# Backend agents: the research workflow as built Status 11 Oct 2026, branch `backend-agents-tavily`. This page shows what the backend agents do today, which data goes where, and how it lines up with the architecture we designed ([`01`](01-system-overview.md), [`05`](05-hitl-map.md), [`07`](07-pm-workflow.md), [`09`](09-scoring-and-memory.md)). Code: `backend/` (see its README) and `web/src/lib/pipeline/research.ts`. **In one sentence:** one agentic step is live, the **research agent** of layer L2. A lead researcher sends two scout sub-agents to search the public web through Tavily's MCP server. The backend checks every source against the real search results and drops the rest. It returns competitor features and market trends, linked to the PM's feature requests, plus a list of what it could not find. Everything else in the pipeline still runs in the web app, mostly as deterministic code. ## 1. One research run, step by step ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor PM as Product manager participant UI as Web · SignalsPanel
/dashboard/[market]/[series] participant API as FastAPI
POST /research/signals participant Lead as lead_researcher
(strong OpenAI model) participant CS as competitor_scout
(fast model) participant TS as trend_scout
(fast model) participant TV as Tavily remote MCP
tavily_search · tavily_extract PM->>UI: Run research agent UI->>API: series · market · feature-request titles
(+ optional focus, categories) API->>Lead: prompt (no customer data) par Harness SubAgents · delegate_task Lead->>CS: competitors for 5 Series · Europe CS->>TV: up to 6 searches (soft budget) TV-->>CS: titles · URLs · snippets (URLs recorded) CS-->>Lead: signals + gaps (JSON) and Lead->>TS: trends + regulation for 5 Series · Europe TS->>TV: up to 6 searches TV-->>TS: titles · URLs · snippets (URLs recorded) TS-->>Lead: signals + gaps (JSON) end Lead->>Lead: merge · dedupe · pick the best ≤ max
link relatesTo to exact request titles · list gaps Lead-->>API: LeadOutput (typed) API->>API: category filter · verify_sources
drop URLs Tavily never returned → gap API-->>UI: ResearchResult · MarketSignal[] · gaps · searches UI->>UI: replaces the saved research for this market + series
(localStorage) → backing, links, score, wishlist, profiles PM->>UI: star (wishlist) · focus · keep / reject requests ``` What makes it trustworthy: - **The agents propose and the PM decides.** The result only changes the "Competitors & trends" panel and the *market backing* part of the Dixi score. Wishlist, keep and reject stay human decisions. - **Sources are checked by code, not by the model.** Every URL Tavily returns is recorded during the run. A source the model wrote that is not among them gets removed, and a signal left without sources is dropped and listed as a gap. - **Honesty is part of the output.** `gaps` lists what the agents searched for and could not back. In the 11 Oct run for the 5 Series in Europe, one gap read: *"Euro NCAP criteria are safety-rating incentives, not binding EU interface law."* - **The budget is bounded.** Each scout gets at most 6 searches at basic depth (1 Tavily credit each), so a run uses at most about 12 credits. Past the budget the search tool answers "budget used up, answer now" instead of aborting the run. ## 2. Which data goes where ```mermaid flowchart LR %% Privacy boundary: BMW data never leaves the machine; only our own titles and public web content reach external services. classDef local fill:#fdecea,stroke:#e22718,color:#121722 classDef ours fill:#eef1f6,stroke:#5b6676,color:#121722 classDef ext fill:#e8f0fc,stroke:#1c69d4,color:#121722 subgraph LOCAL["This machine only (git-ignored)"] BMW[("data/ · BMW dataset
feedback verbatims · studies · sales · option list")]:::local SCR["scripts/build-pipeline-data.py
deterministic: taxonomy → 25 clusters
no network, no LLM"]:::local PJ[("web/data-local/pipeline.json
counts · scores · sales · options · ≤3 quotes")]:::local end WEB["Web app (Next.js)
urgency · score · decisions · profiles
all computed in code"]:::ours EX[("example.ts
same shape, example data
used on Vercel")]:::ours OAI["OpenAI API
research agents · scoring advice"]:::ext TAV["Tavily
web search"]:::ext WWW["Public web
press · regulators · market research"]:::ext BMW --> SCR --> PJ --> WEB EX --> WEB WEB -- "series · market · our request titles · focus" --> OAI WEB -- "a manager's instruction + scoring settings" --> OAI OAI -- "search queries written by the scouts" --> TAV --> WWW TAV -- "public snippets + URLs" --> OAI ``` **What the BMW data is used for, and what is not sent anywhere:** | BMW data | How it is used today | Leaves the machine? | |---|---|---| | Customer feedback (verbatims, taxonomy, feedback type, market) | `build-pipeline-data.py` maps BMW's taxonomy topics to 25 PM-friendly clusters with hand-written titles, counts unique mentions per market and type, and keeps ≤ 3 short quotes per request for the local screen | **No.** Quotes stay in `pipeline.json`. Only our own cluster *titles* (e.g. "Simpler iDrive menus and touchscreen") go to OpenAI, so the research agent can link signals to them | | Customer studies (CN/EU 0–10, US 1–7) | Weakest-score panel; US converted ×10/7 | No | | Sales 2024/2025/2030 | Market volume, fallback logic, sales table | No | | Option list (Germany, July 2026) | Related options per request, profile option totals | No | | Competitors and trends | **Not BMW data.** Public web only: the saved research (`market-signals.ts`, 10 Oct) or a live run (backend) | Search queries go to Tavily, and public results come back | **What "AI analysis" means today, honestly:** the analysis screen narrates the steps of the pipeline. Behind it, clustering, categories and urgency come from the deterministic script and the web code, **not from an LLM**. Only the research agent (this page) and the natural-language scoring settings ([`09`](09-scoring-and-memory.md)) call a model. LLM labelling of verbatims is planned (§4). It would be the first time customer text is sent to OpenAI, so it needs a decision first (§5). ## 3. Designed architecture vs what is built | Designed step (doc) | Mode in the design | Built today | Where | |---|---|---|---| | Research agent: competitor features + trends, with sources ([01](01-system-overview.md), [07](07-pm-workflow.md)) | AI proposes | ✅ **Live**: lead + 2 scout sub-agents, Tavily MCP, source check, gaps. Saved research as fallback | `backend/app/agents/research.py`, `web/src/lib/pipeline/research.ts` | | Link requests ↔ competitors / trends ([07](07-pm-workflow.md)) | AI on its own | ✅ Live runs: the lead fills `relatesTo` with exact request titles. Saved research: links written by hand | backend lead agent | | Collect sources ([05](05-hitl-map.md)) | AI on its own | ✅ for public web (Tavily). BMW data: local loader script | backend · `scripts/` | | Cluster feedback into feature requests ([01](01-system-overview.md)) | AI on its own | 🟡 **Deterministic** taxonomy mapping, no LLM. Planned: LLM labeller + clusterer | `scripts/build-pipeline-data.py` | | Categorise Exterior · Interior · Digital · Powertrain | AI on its own | 🟡 Requests: fixed per cluster in the script. Signals: chosen by the agents, filterable via `categories` | script · backend | | Urgency (how many customers ask) | AI on its own | ✅ Code, not AI (mention thresholds) | `web/src/lib/pipeline/profiles.ts` | | Dixi score + decision memory ([09](09-scoring-and-memory.md)) | AI proposes, rules set by team | ✅ in the web app (localStorage). Backend `get_decision_memory` + pgvector: planned | `web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts` | | PM gate: keep · reject + reason · priority · wishlist | Human only | ✅ web (localStorage) | `Pipeline.tsx` | | Build 3 profiles | AI proposes | ✅ deterministic builder in the web app | `profiles.ts` | | Requirement writer (SMART drafts) ([05](05-hitl-map.md)) | AI proposes ~90 % | ⚪ Not built | planned `backend/app/agents/` | | Gates G1–G4, engineering check, Codebeamer hand-off ([05](05-hitl-map.md)) | Human / AI proposes | ⚪ Not built | target state | | L3 social test | AI on its own | 🟡 Simulated in the web app | `analytics.ts` | | Store: evidence, decisions, generations, research runs | — | 🟡 localStorage. Supabase project **Dixi** exists, no schema yet | planned `supabase/` | **Where it differs from the design:** 1. The design places the research agent *before* the analysis as an input to L2. In the app it is a **PM-triggered** step on the review screen, because a run takes about a minute and spends credits. The saved research fills the gap until it is run. 2. The design says the AI clusters feedback. Today a script does it deterministically. That is more explainable but less flexible (§4). 3. Research runs are not stored server-side yet, so the run that backed a decision lives only in that browser. For full auditability ([08](08-decision-audit.md)) a run should be saved with its inputs and linked from the generation. ## 4. Frontend parts that use the research agent | Part | What changed | |---|---| | `lib/pipeline/research.ts` (new) | `runResearch()` calls `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL/research/signals`; `useResearch(market, series)` keeps the last run per market + series in localStorage and gives signals stable ids (`R-`), so a wishlist star survives a re-run | | `components/pipeline/SignalsPanel.tsx` | Shows provenance ("Saved research" or "Live research · time · N web searches"), **Run research agent** / **Run again** / **Use saved research**, errors, and **What we couldn't find** (the agents' gaps) | | `components/pipeline/Pipeline.tsx` | Signals come from the live run when there is one, else from `market-signals.ts`. Everything downstream uses the same list: backing in the score, matching badges, *Backed by market* filter, wishlist, profiles (wishes + backing), header count | | `components/pipeline/SignalCount.tsx` (new) → `SeriesPicker.tsx` | Signal count on each series card follows the last live run ("· live") | | Not touched | Landing, globe, generations, settings: they do not use market signals. Saved generations keep the signals they were built with | Live research runs for **Europe, USA and China** one market at a time (the backend's markets). For *All markets* and *Japan* the button explains why it is disabled. Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (the public Vercel deployment today), the app uses the saved research. ## 5. Next steps (recommended order) 1. **Deploy** the backend to FastAPI Cloud and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` on Vercel ([backend README](../../backend/README.md#deploy-fastapi-cloud-public-beta)). 2. **Store research runs** in Supabase (`research_run`: inputs, model, searches, signals, gaps, sources) and link a generation to the run it used. That closes the audit gap in §3.3. 3. **Decision memory in the backend**: `get_decision_memory(series, market)` as a tool for the next agent, same rules as `scoring.ts`, with pgvector matching ([09](09-scoring-and-memory.md)). 4. **Requirement writer** agent: SMART drafts per kept request, citing the request's evidence and the signals behind it (G1 → draft in [05](05-hitl-map.md)). 5. **LLM labelling of BMW feedback**: only once the team confirms that BMW customer text may be sent to OpenAI. OpenAI states it does not train on API data by default (https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/), but sending the text is still a data-sharing decision for BMW. Until then, keep the deterministic script.

(localStorage) → backing, links, score, wishlist, profiles PM->>UI: star (wishlist) · focus · keep / reject requests ``` What makes it trustworthy: - **The agents propose and the PM decides.** The result only changes the "Competitors & trends" panel and the *market backing* part of the Dixi score. Dixi helps a BMW product manager turn what each market says into car profiles for the next 1, 5 or 7 Series, and keeps the reason for every decision. Inputs sit in three layers: **L1 BMW principles** (the fundamentals of each series, owned by managers), **L2 market evidence** (customer feedback and feature requests, customer studies, sales, today's option list, plus a research agent that adds competitor features people like and market trends, each with sources) and **L3 social test** (runs only after profiles exist: which profile tracks better on social media; low weight per series: 7 Series 2 %, 5 Series 8 %, 1 Series 20 %). The PM picks a market and a series; AI clusters the evidence into feature requests by category and urgency; the PM keeps or rejects each one (a reject needs a reason), drags them into priority order and wishlists competitor or trend features. Dixi then builds three profiles that follow that priority (score = L1 principles + priority fit, plus L2 coverage) and saves the build as a **generation** with its profiles, decisions and priority. Every decision records who made it (name and role, from a simple local identity until there is a login) and when, and shows up in the decision log, the profile's decision trail and its PDF. Today decisions, priority and generations live in the browser (localStorage); BMW-derived data stays local and git-ignored, and the public deployment runs on example data. content.text:
The new doc is `docs/architecture/10-backend-agents.md`. The frontend now runs the live research agent, and I checked it end to end in the browser. To your data question: BMW's customer data is used, but only on your machine, and none of it is sent to OpenAI.

**How the backend works today.** Only the research agent (layer L2) is live:
1. The PM clicks **Run research agent**.
2. A lead agent sends two sub-agents in parallel, one for competitors and one for trends.
3. Each sub-agent runs up to 6 web searches through the Tavily MCP.
4. The lead merges and de-duplicates what they found and links each signal to the PM's feature requests.
5. Code then removes any source URL that Tavily never actually returned, and the dashboard shows the result.

The doc has this as a step-by-step diagram.

**Does it match the architecture we designed?** Mostly, and the doc has a full "designed vs built" table. Three differences you should know about:
- **Research is started by the PM.** The design has it running before the analysis. In the app the PM starts it, because a run takes about a minute and costs search credits. The saved research is shown until then.
- **"AI analysis" isn't AI yet.** The design says an AI groups customer feedback into feature requests. Today a script does it with fixed rules (BMW's topic labels mapped to 25 requests). The analysis screen only narrates the steps.
- **Research runs aren't stored on a server.** They live only in that browser, so a decision can't yet be traced back to the run that backed it. Saving runs in Supabase is next on the list.

**Your data question:**
- **BMW customer data:** a local script turns it into counts, scores and up to 3 short quotes per request, with no AI and no network. That file is git-ignored and never leaves your machine. The quotes, study scores, sales and option list are not sent anywhere.
- **What does reach OpenAI:**
  - the series, the market and our own request titles (written by hand, e.g. "Simpler iDrive menus and touchscreen"), sent by the research agent;
  - a manager's plain-words instruction for the scoring settings.
- **Competitors and trends:** these are not BMW data. They come from the public web, either the saved research from 10 Oct or a live run. Only the search queries the agents write go to Tavily.
- **Decision for you:** using AI on the customer comments themselves would be the first time BMW customer text goes to OpenAI. OpenAI says it doesn't train on API data by default (https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/), but sending the text is still BMW's call. I recommend confirming with BMW first.

**Frontend changes**
- **"Competitors & trends" panel:** shows whether the results are live (time and number of searches) or saved, and has **Run research agent**, **Run again** and **Use saved research** buttons. It also has a **What we couldn't find** list from the agents and shows errors.
- **Pipeline:** a live run replaces the saved research everywhere signals are used: the score, the match badges, the "Backed by market" filter, the wishlist, the profiles and the header count. Wishlist stars survive a re-run.
- **Series cards:** the signal count follows the last live run.
- **Scope:** live runs cover Europe, USA and China, one market at a time. For Japan and "All markets" the button explains why it's disabled.
- **Untouched:** landing, globe, generations and settings, because they don't use market signals.

**Browser test (5 Series, Europe):** 6 live signals, each with a real source (Mercedes E-Class press, Euro NCAP, an EU charging-infrastructure regulation, Audi media), plus 7 gaps and no console errors. Scores re-ranked from the new backing.

I also updated docs 01, 06, 07 and the docs index, plus `web/.env.example`. Everything is pushed to `backend-agents-tavily`.

To make "Run research agent" work in production, the backend still needs deploying: run `! cd backend && uv run fastapi login` and I'll deploy it and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` on Vercel. Changing Vercel environment variables needs your OK, so I'll confirm with you first.

# BMW Group General Market Principles — Four-Market Research

These are principle-focused research documents, not general market reports or research prompts.

- `bmw_uk_general_principles.md` — UK market principles.
- `bmw_china_general_principles.md` — China market principles.
- `bmw_us_general_principles.md` — United States market principles.
- `bmw_europe_general_principles.md` — Europe market principles.
- `bmw_global_principles_across_four_markets.md` — shared BMW Group principles and how they differ in application.

The reports separate principles BMW explicitly states from repeated practice and evidence-supported interpretation. Concrete facts appear only as evidence for a principle. They do not claim to reveal unpublished internal practices or pretend BMW operated in all four markets for 100 years. BMW's car production dates to 1928, while documented market histories begin at different times.
# BMW Group — General Principles Across the UK, China, United States and Europe

**Purpose:** Separate the principles BMW Group explicitly states for the whole company from the ways those principles appear in four market contexts.

**Evidence cut-off:** 10 October 2026

## Historical boundary: what “about 100 years” means

BMW Group traces its corporate origins to 1916, but BMW entered automobile production in 1928. BMW did not sell BMW-branded cars in all four markets for 100 years: BMW of North America began operations in 1975; BMW's dedicated sales-subsidiary transition began in major markets in 1973; BMW says it has been in China since 1994 and founded BMW Brilliance in 2003. Therefore, the correct research question is: **Which Group-level principles formed over BMW's history, and how are they applied differently where each market's evidence permits?** [S1][S2][S3][S4]

## Group-level principles BMW explicitly states

### 1. Global footprint, locally informed decisions

BMW identifies its production, R&D, sales and supplier networks as a core strength. It says long-term presence helps the Group understand local customer needs and use capabilities from local R&D networks, universities, IT hubs and technology partners. [S2]

**Application pattern:** UK—local sales organisation and retailer support; China—local production, R&D and technology partnerships; US—national sales organisation and major manufacturing/export base; Europe—regional scale combined with national differences.

### 2. Production follows the market, but not mechanically

BMW says market proximity is one criterion for deciding which models are built where. It explicitly notes US production for the X-family, China production mainly serving Chinese demand, and German plants making models mainly sold in Europe. BMW also describes a globally balanced production network. [S3][S5]

**Principle:** Place production where demand, product specialisation, supplier networks, cost, logistics and strategic resilience justify it. This does not mean every sales market must manufacture every car locally.

### 3. Technology neutrality and customer-driven drivetrain choice

BMW describes its strategy as following market demand and customer needs while optimising drivetrain variants, and it states that the pace of electromobility differs between markets. [S2]

**Principle:** Do not assume all markets and customers transition to a new technology at the same pace. Continue adapting the powertrain portfolio while meeting applicable law and assessing profitability.

### 4. Global product identity with selected local adaptation

BMW says its broad portfolio is meant to meet customer needs globally, and it emphasises identifying trends in individual markets early. The China statements “in China for China” and “in China, for China, with China” show how far local adaptation can go in one especially distinctive market. [S2][S4]

**Principle:** Preserve the core brand and group-wide engineering responsibility while letting local needs meaningfully influence product configuration, digital experience and commercial approach.

### 5. Balance brand value and volume

BMW explicitly says it seeks a healthy balance of value and volume in major regions. [S2]

**Principle:** Scale matters in mass manufacturing, but maximising unit volume alone can dilute premium positioning or destroy value. Conversely, premium positioning must be paired with enough demand and factory/channel utilisation.

### 6. Flexible, standardised production

BMW's iFACTORY framework is described as LEAN. GREEN. DIGITAL.: efficient, precise and flexible processes; resource optimisation and circularity; and digital systems/data. # BMW in Europe — Evidence-Based Regional Market Study

**Research cut-off:** 10 October 2026  
**Scope:** Europe is a region, not a synonym for the EU. EU-wide law, national policies, non-EU European markets and the UK's separate regulatory regime are treated distinctly.

## Executive findings

1. **Europe was BMW Group's largest reported sales region in 2025.** BMW Group reported 1,016,360 BMW/MINI deliveries in its Europe region, up 7.3%. Germany alone accounted for 290,742, up 8.7%. BMW says Europe deliveries passed one million for the first time since 2019. These are BMW Group regional delivery figures, not registrations for EU27 or BMW-brand-only totals. [S1]
2. **EU powertrain adoption in 2025 did not equate to BEV-only demand.** ACEA reports new EU registrations rose 1.8%; BEVs reached 17.4% share, hybrids 34.5%, plug-in hybrids 9.4%, and petrol plus diesel 35.5%. These are market-level registration statistics and should not be compared directly to BMW regional deliveries without noting scope and period. [S2]
3. **BMW-reported European BEV deliveries accelerated in Q2 2026.** BMW said its Europe sales region delivered 81,500 BEVs in Q2 2026, up 37.9% year-on-year, and BEVs represented 31.3% of its deliveries in that region. This is a quarterly company-region measure, not the EU's annual market share. [S3]
4. **EU CO₂ standards are manufacturer fleet-level rules, not a simple rule that each car model must be electric today.** The Commission lists EU-wide fleet targets for cars of 93.6 g CO₂/km for 2025–2029 and 49.5 g/km for 2030–2034, with 0 g/km from 2035 under the current framework described on its website. Regulation (EU) 2025/1214 adopted additional flexibility to average compliance over 2025–2027. The Commission's December 2025 Automotive Package included proposals; a proposal should not be treated as enacted law without checking later legislative status. [S4][S5][S6]
5. **Europe cannot be analysed as one cultural or tax market.** Germany alone had 290,742 BMW/MINI deliveries in 2025, while company-car taxation, purchase incentives, charging networks, fleet composition and national regulations differ across countries. EU-wide market data and BMW's company-defined Europe region have different geographic coverage. [S1][S2]

## 1. Regional market and BMW data

| Metric | Value | Period and scope | Limitation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| BMW Group BMW/MINI deliveries in Europe | 1,016,360 | 2025 BMW sales region | +7.3% YoY; BMW Group definition [S1] |
| BMW Group deliveries in Germany | 290,742 | 2025 | +8.7%; subset of Europe, do not add to it [S1] |
| BMW Group Europe deliveries | +5.4% | H1 2026 | Group region; not EU registration totals [S3] |
| BMW Group Europe BEV deliveries | 81,500 | Q2 2026 | +37.9% YoY; 31.3% of BMW Group regional deliveries [S3] |
| EU new-car registrations | +1.8% | 2025 | ACEA EU passenger car registrations [S2] |
| EU BEV market share | 17.4% | 2025 | Up from 13.6% in 2024 [S2] |
| EU hybrid-electric share | 34.5% | 2025 | ACEA's largest power category [S2] |
| EU plug-in hybrid share | 9.4% | 2025 | Up from 7.2% in 2024 [S2] |
| EU petrol + diesel share | 35.5% | 2025 | Down from 45.2% in 2024 [S2] |
| BMW Group global deliveries | 2,463,715 | 2025 | +0.5%; all Group automotive deliveries [S1] |

## 2. Timeline: strategy and regulatory framework

| Date | Event | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| 1973 onward | BMW started reclaiming sales responsibility from independent importers and creating BMW-owned sales subsidiaries in major markets. [S7] | Group-level move toward direct market organizations; national execution varies. |
| 2019 | Regulation (EU) 2019/631 established the core EU framework for CO₂ emission performance standards for new cars and vans. [S4] | Manufacturer fleet-average obligations, rather than a universal drivetrain rule for every individual model. |
| 2023 | Commission implementing decision set manufacturer-specific targets using EU-wide fleet targets and calculation rules. [S4] | Manufacturer targets depend on formula and fleet characteristics. |
| 2025 | EU BEV share reached 17.4%, hybrid-electric 34.5%; BMW Group Europe deliveries rose 7.3%. [S1][S2] | Electrification and divergent powertrain demand coexist. |
| 17 June 2025 | Regulation (EU) 2025/1214 amended CO₂ compliance calculation to allow a weighted three-year averaging period for 2025–2027. [S5] | Flexibility was adopted into binding law while targets remained. |
| 16 Dec 2025 | European Commission presented an automotive package including a proposal to revise parts of the 2035 CO₂ framework. [S6] | Proposal status needs checking against any subsequent adopted act. |
| Q2 2026 | BMW Group reported Europe BEV deliveries up 37.9% to 81,500, 31.3% of its deliveries in the region. [S3] | Company-reported quarterly outcome. |
| 2026 | Neue Klasse rollout began, with BMW saying new technology clusters will be applied across more models. [S3][S8] | Product-generation transition; long-term profitability and customer response still need model-level evidence. |

  Manage Postgres databases.

USAGE
  supabase db <subcommand> [flags]

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h                Show help information
  --version, -v             Show version information
  --completions choice      Print shell completion script (choices: bash, zsh, fish, sh)
  --log-level choice        Sets the minimum log level (choices: all, trace, debug, info, warn, warning, error, fatal, none)
  --output-format choice    Output format: text (default), json, or stream-json (NDJSON) (choices: text, json, stream-json)
  --output, -o choice       Output format of status variables. (choices: env, pretty, json, toml, yaml)

  --workdir string          Path to a Supabase project directory.
  --experimental            Enable experimental features.
  --network-id string       Use the specified Docker network instead of a generated one.

  pull        Pull schema from the remote database

  lint        Checks local database for typing error

  --skip-pooler            Use direct connection instead of pooler.

# BMW Group — General Market Principles: Europe

**Purpose:** Identify BMW Group's general principles for serving Europe as a region of connected but non-identical national markets, rather than catalogue individual regulations or country-specific models.

**Evidence cut-off:** 10 October 2026  
**Scope note:** Europe is not synonymous with the European Union. EU rules, national tax and customer conditions, the UK's separate framework, and non-EU European markets must be distinguished. BMW's longer history in Germany cannot automatically be applied to all European countries.

## What counts as a principle

- **Explicit BMW principle:** stated directly by BMW.
- **Repeated documented practice:** recurring operating pattern established by real decisions.
- **Evidence-supported interpretation:** careful conclusion from documented behaviour; not BMW's own language.

## Defensible general principles

### EU-01 — Treat Europe as a regional system made up of different national markets

**Classification:** Evidence-supported interpretation of BMW's stated market approach and regional footprint. **Confidence:** High.

BMW Group says its international presence enables it to understand specific customer needs in individual markets. It reports regional sales and country activity separately, and its European network includes production sites with different roles. [S1][S2]

**General principle:** Use regional scale for platforms, engineering, brand and supply-chain coordination, but do not assume one product mix, retail model, tax environment or customer preference applies identically across every European country.

**Boundary:** BMW's public sources support local-market awareness, but do not reveal the full level of decision autonomy assigned to every country organisation. This is an interpretation of the operating model.

### EU-02 — Combine global brand consistency with local customer adaptation

**Classification:** Explicit Group-wide approach plus repeated documented practice. **Confidence:** High.

input.command:
cd /Volumes/PJ/peresjav/hackathons/ehl-final-minuch-2026 && supabase migration new core_schema >/dev/null && f=$(ls supabase/migrations/*core_schema.sql) && cat > $f <<'EOF'
-- Dixi core schema: L1 principles, decisions (append-only history), generations, agent runs, scoring settings.
-- Only the backend (secret key) reads and writes; RLS is on with no policies, so the public anon key gets nothing.
-- BMW customer data (verbatims, quotes) is never stored here: requests are referenced by id + title only.

-- L1 principles: Group-wide, per market (research in data/L1_Files) and per series (product fundamentals).
create table public.principles (
  id             text primary key,                 -- 'GL-01', 'EU-03', 'UK-04', 'CN-05', 'US-07', 'G60-P1'
  level          text not null check (level in ('group', 'market', 'series')),
  market         text check (market in ('GLOBAL', 'EU', 'UK', 'CN', 'US')),
  series         text check (series in ('F70', 'G60', 'G70')),
  title          text not null,
  statement      text not null,                    -- the principle itself
  boundary       text,                             -- what it does not say / must not be inferred
  classification text,                             -- explicit BMW principle · repeated practice · interpretation
  confidence     text,                             -- High · Medium · Low (from the research)
  sources        jsonb not null default '[]',      -- [{ref, label, url}]
  owner          text not null,                    -- who may change it
  version        int  not null default 1,
  active         boolean not null default true,
  updated_at     timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_by     text not null default 'seed'
);
create index principles_market_idx on public.principles (market) where active;
create index principles_series_idx on public.principles (series) where active;

-- Every PM decision, append-only: an undo is its own row, so the history is never lost.
create table public.decisions (
  id            bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  series        text not null check (series in ('F70', 'G60', 'G70')),
  market        text not null,                     -- app scope: EU · US · CN · JP · ALL
  request_id    text not null,                     -- feature request or signal id
  title         text not null,
  action        text not null check (action in ('keep', 'reject', 'wish', 'undo')),
  reason        text,
  mentions_at   int,                               -- customer mentions at decision time (resurfacing rule)
  by_name       text not null,
  by_role       text,
  at            timestamptz not null default now(),
  generation_id text,                              -- set when the decision was saved with a build
  constraint reject_needs_reason check (action <> 'reject' or length(coalesce(trim(reason), '')) > 0)
);
create index decisions_lookup_idx on public.decisions (series, market, request_id, at desc);

-- Generations: every "Build profiles" (profiles, decisions, priority, social test) as the web app's Session object.
create table public.generations (
  id              text primary key,                -- 'G-…'
  series          text not null,
  market          text not null,
  created_at      timestamptz not null,
  created_by      text,
  created_by_role text,
  payload         jsonb not null,
  updated_at      timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index generations_series_idx on public.generations (series, market, created_at desc);

-- Agent runs, stored with their inputs and outputs so every signal and assessment can be traced.
create table public.research_runs (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  series      text not null,
  market      text not null,
  request     jsonb not null,
  result      jsonb not null,
  model       text not null,
  searches    int  not null,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index research_runs_idx on public.research_runs (series, market, created_at desc);

create table public.principle_assessments (
  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  series          text not null,
  market          text not null,
  principle_ids   text[] not null,                 -- the principles the agent was given (snapshot of ids)
  request         jsonb not null,
  result          jsonb not null,
  model           text not null,
  created_at      timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index principle_assessments_idx on public.principle_assessments (series, market, created_at desc);

-- Scoring settings (one row today; per-series rows later) and the log of every applied change.
create table public.scoring_settings (
  id          text primary key default 'global',
  settings    jsonb not null,
  updated_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_by  text not null
);

create table public.scoring_changes (
  id          bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  instruction text,                                -- the manager's words, if any
  source      text not null,                       -- 'sliders' · 'ai:<model>' · 'rules'
  changes     jsonb not null,                      -- ["wDemand 0.6 → 0.5 because …"]
  before      jsonb not null,
  after       jsonb not null,
  by_name     text not null,
  by_role     text,
  at          timestamptz not null default now()
);

alter table public.principles            enable row level security;
alter table public.decisions             enable row level security;
alter table public.generations           enable row level security;
alter table public.research_runs         enable row level security;
alter table public.principle_assessments enable row level security;
alter table public.scoring_settings      enable row level security;
alter table public.scoring_changes       enable row level security;
EOF
echo $f; sed -i '' 's|^/supabase/.temp|&|' .gitignore; grep -n "supabase" .gitignore

The web app ranks with the TypeScript version; the backend uses this one to give the agents the same memory the PM sees.

"""
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Literal

from app.models.core import ScoringSettings


def memory_key(series: str, title: str) -> str:
    return f"{series}:{title.lower()}"


@dataclass
class MemoryEntry:
    action: Literal["keep", "reject"]
    reason: str | None
    by: str
    role: str | None
    at: str
    mentionsAt: int | None
    generationId: str
    scopeLabel: str


def build_memory(generations: list[dict[str, Any]], series: str, scope: str, s: ScoringSettings) -> dict[str, MemoryEntry]:
    """Latest keep/reject per request from earlier generations (web Session payloads) of this series and market."""
    mem: dict[str, MemoryEntry] = {}
    relevant = sorted(
        (g for g in generations if g.get("series") == series and (s.memoryScope == "all" or g.get("scope") == scope)),
        key=lambda g: g.get("createdAt", ""),
    )
    for g in relevant:
        for d in (g.get("decisions") or {}).values():
            if d.get("action") not in ("keep", "reject"):
                continue
            k = memory_key(series, d["title"])
            prev = mem.get(k)
            if prev is None or prev.at <= d["at"]:
                mem[k] = MemoryEntry(
                    action=d["action"], reason=d.get("reason"), by=d.get("by", ""), role=d.get("role"), at=d["at"],
                    mentionsAt=d.get("mentionsAt"), generationId=g["id"], scopeLabel=g.get("scopeLabel", g.get("scope", "")),
                )
    return mem


@dataclass
class Scored:
    score: int
    base: int
    demand: float
    backing: float
    fit: float
    state: Literal["rejected", "resurfaced", "kept"] | None
    strength: float
    growth: float | None
    hidden: bool


def _days_since(iso: str, now: datetime) -> float:
    at = datetime.fromisoformat(iso.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    return max(0.0, (now - at).total_seconds() / 86_400)


def score_request(
    series: str, title: str, category: str, scoped: int, max_scoped: int, backing_count: int,
    focus: list[str], memory: dict[str, MemoryEntry], s: ScoringSettings,
    now: datetime | None = None, fit: float | None = None,
) -> Scored:
    """`fit` = principle fit from the principle assessor (0–1); without one, the series-focus fallback is used."""
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    demand = math.log1p(scoped) / math.log1p(max_scoped) if max_scoped > 0 else 0.0
    backing = min(1.0, backing_count / 2)
    fit = fit if fit is not None else (1.0 if category in focus else 0.4)
    w_sum = (s.wDemand + s.wBacking + s.wFit) or 1
    base = 100 * (s.wDemand * demand + s.wBacking * backing + s.wFit * fit) / w_sum

    m = memory.get(memory_key(series, title))
    state, strength, growth, score = None, 0.0, None, base
    if m:
        strength = 0.5 ** (_days_since(m.at, now) / max(1, s.halfLifeDays))
        growth = (scoped - m.mentionsAt) / m.mentionsAt if m.mentionsAt else None
        if m.action == "reject":
            resurfaced = growth is not None and growth >= s.resurfaceAt
            state = "resurfaced" if resurfaced else "rejected"
            if not resurfaced:
                score = base * (1 - s.rejectPenalty * strength)
        else:
            state = "kept"
            score = min(100.0, base + 10 * s.keepBonus * strength)
    return Scored(

    return math.floor(x + 0.5)

"""Storage for principles, decisions, generations, agent runs and scoring settings.

SupabaseStore talks to the hosted project through its REST API (PostgREST) with the backend-only secret key;
schema in supabase/migrations. MemoryStore has the same interface for tests and for running without Supabase.
"""
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Protocol

import httpx

from app.config import Settings
from app.models.core import Decision, DecisionIn, Generation, Principle, PrincipleEdit, ScoringSettings, SettingsState, SettingsUpdate


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


class Store(Protocol):
    kind: str

    async def list_principles(self, markets: list[str], series: str | None) -> list[Principle]: ...
    async def upsert_principles(self, rows: list[Principle]) -> int: ...
    async def edit_principle(self, pid: str, edit: PrincipleEdit) -> Principle | None: ...
    async def add_decision(self, d: DecisionIn) -> Decision: ...
    async def list_decisions(self, series: str, market: str | None) -> list[Decision]: ...
    async def save_generation(self, g: Generation) -> None: ...
    async def list_generations(self, series: str | None = None) -> list[Generation]: ...
    async def delete_generation(self, gid: str) -> None: ...
    async def save_run(self, table: str, row: dict[str, Any]) -> str: ...
    async def latest_run(self, table: str, series: str, market: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None: ...
    async def get_settings(self) -> SettingsState: ...
    async def save_settings(self, u: SettingsUpdate) -> SettingsState: ...
    async def list_setting_changes(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: ...


def _principle_filter(p: Principle, markets: list[str], series: str | None) -> bool:
    if not p.active:
        return False
    if p.level == "series":
        return series is not None and p.series == series
    return p.market in markets


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- in memory


class MemoryStore:
    kind = "memory"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.principles: dict[str, Principle] = {}
        self.decisions: list[Decision] = []
        self.generations: dict[str, Generation] = {}
        self.runs: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {"research_runs": [], "principle_assessments": []}
        self.settings = SettingsState(settings=ScoringSettings())
        self.changes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    async def list_principles(self, markets, series):
        return sorted((p for p in self.principles.values() if _principle_filter(p, markets, series)), key=lambda p: p.id)

    async def upsert_principles(self, rows):
        for p in rows:
            self.principles[p.id] = p
        return len(rows)

    async def edit_principle(self, pid, edit):
        p = self.principles.get(pid)
        if not p:
            return None
        p = p.model_copy(update={"statement": edit.statement, "boundary": edit.boundary, "version": p.version + 1,
                                 "updated_by": edit.by, "updated_at": _now()})
        self.principles[pid] = p
        return p

    async def add_decision(self, d):
        if d.action == "reject" and not (d.reason or "").strip():
            raise ValueError("A reject needs a reason")
        row = Decision(id=len(self.decisions) + 1, **d.model_dump(exclude={"at"}), at=d.at or _now())
        self.decisions.append(row)
        return row

    async def list_decisions(self, series, market):
        return [d for d in self.decisions if d.series == series and (market is None or d.market == market)]

    async def save_generation(self, g):
        self.generations[g.id] = g

    async def list_generations(self, series=None):
        gs = [g for g in self.generations.values() if series is None or g.series == series]
        return sorted(gs, key=lambda g: g.createdAt, reverse=True)

    async def delete_generation(self, gid):
        self.generations.pop(gid, None)

    async def save_run(self, table, row):
        rid = f"{table}-{len(self.runs[table]) + 1}"
        self.runs[table].append({"id": rid, "created_at": _now(), **row})
        return rid

    async def latest_run(self, table, series, market):
        rows = [r for r in self.runs[table] if r["series"] == series and r["market"] == market]
        return rows[-1] if rows else None

    async def get_settings(self):
        return self.settings

    async def save_settings(self, u):
        before = self.settings.settings
        self.settings = SettingsState(settings=u.settings, updatedAt=_now(), updatedBy=u.by)
        self.changes.append({"instruction": u.instruction, "source": u.source, "changes": u.changes,
                             "before": before.model_dump(), "after": u.settings.model_dump(),
                             "by_name": u.by, "by_role": u.role, "at": _now()})
        return self.settings

    async def list_setting_changes(self, limit=50):
        return list(reversed(self.changes))[:limit]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Supabase


class SupabaseStore:
    kind = "supabase"

    def __init__(self, url: str, key: str) -> None:
        headers = {"apikey": key, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if key.startswith("eyJ"):  # legacy service_role JWT also goes in Authorization; new sb_secret_ keys do not
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {key}"
        self.http = httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=f"{url.rstrip('/')}/rest/v1", headers=headers, timeout=20)

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        await self.http.aclose()

    async def _get(self, table: str, params: dict[str, str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        r = await self.http.get(f"/{table}", params=params)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()

    async def _post(self, table: str, rows: Any, upsert: bool = False) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        prefer = "return=representation" + (",resolution=merge-duplicates" if upsert else "")
        r = await self.http.post(f"/{table}", json=rows, headers={"Prefer": prefer})
        if r.status_code >= 400:
            raise ValueError(f"Supabase {table}: {r.status_code} {r.text[:300]}")
        return r.json()

    async def list_principles(self, markets, series):
        rows = await self._get("principles", {"select": "*", "active": "eq.true", "order": "id"})
        return [p for p in (Principle.model_validate(r) for r in rows) if _principle_filter(p, markets, series)]

    async def upsert_principles(self, rows):
        out = await self._post("principles", [p.model_dump(exclude={"updated_at"}) for p in rows], upsert=True)
        return len(out)

    async def edit_principle(self, pid, edit):
        cur = await self._get("principles", {"select": "version", "id": f"eq.{pid}"})
        if not cur:
            return None
        r = await self.http.patch(
            "/principles", params={"id": f"eq.{pid}"}, headers={"Prefer": "return=representation"},
            json={"statement": edit.statement, "boundary": edit.boundary, "version": cur[0]["version"] + 1,
                  "updated_by": edit.by, "updated_at": _now()},
        )
        r.raise_for_status()

import asyncio
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from app.config import get_settings  # noqa: E402
from app.db import SupabaseStore, make_store  # noqa: E402
from app.models.core import Principle, Source  # noqa: E402

SERIES_TS = ROOT / "web" / "src" / "lib" / "pipeline" / "series.ts"

                "CN": "bmw_china_general_principles.md", "US": "bmw_us_general_principles.md"}
OWNERS = {"GLOBAL": "Group strategy", "EU": "Region Europe", "UK": "BMW UK", "CN": "BMW China", "US": "BMW of North America"}


def clean(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.replace("**", "")).strip()


def sources_of(md: str) -> dict[str, Source]:
    """'- **[S1] Label:** description. https://…' lines of the source register."""
    out = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r"^- \*\*\[(S\d+)\]\s*(.+?):?\*\*:?(.*)$", md, re.M):
        ref, label, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2).rstrip(":"), m.group(3)
        url = re.search(r"https?://\S+", rest)
        out[ref] = Source(ref=ref, label=clean(label), url=url.group(0).rstrip(".,)") if url else None)
    return out


def field(block: str, name: str) -> str | None:
    m = re.search(rf"\*\*{name}:\*\*\s*(.+?)(?=\n\s*\n|\Z)", block, re.S)
    return clean(m.group(1)) if m else None


def cited(text: str, register: dict[str, Source]) -> list[Source]:
    refs = dict.fromkeys(re.findall(r"\[(S\d+)\]", text))
    return [register[r] for r in refs if r in register]


def market_principles(market: str, md: str) -> list[Principle]:
    register = sources_of(md)
    rows = []
    for m in re.finditer(r"^### ([A-Z]{2}-\d{2}) — (.+?)\n(.*?)(?=^### |^## |\Z)", md, re.S | re.M):
        pid, title, block = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip(), m.group(3)
        cls = re.search(r"\*\*Classification:\*\*\s*(.+?)\s*\*\*Confidence:\*\*\s*(\w+)", block)
        paras = [p for p in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", block.strip()) if p.strip() and not p.lstrip().startswith("**")]
        rows.append(Principle(
            id=pid, level="market", market=market, title=title,
            statement=field(block, "General principle") or clean(paras[0] if paras else title),
            evidence=clean(" ".join(paras)) or None, boundary=field(block, "Boundary"),
            classification=clean(cls.group(1)).rstrip(".") if cls else None, confidence=cls.group(2) if cls else None,
            sources=cited(block, register), owner=OWNERS[market],
        ))
    return rows


def group_principles(md: str) -> list[Principle]:
    register = sources_of(md)

    for m in re.finditer(r"^### (\d+)\. (.+?)\n(.*?)(?=^### |^## |\Z)", md, re.S | re.M):

import asyncio
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from app.config import get_settings  # noqa: E402
from app.db import SupabaseStore, make_store  # noqa: E402
from app.models.core import Principle, Source  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
L1 = ROOT / "data" / "L1_Files"
SERIES_TS = ROOT / "web" / "src" / "lib" / "pipeline" / "series.ts"

                "CN": "bmw_china_general_principles.md", "US": "bmw_us_general_principles.md"}
OWNERS = {"GLOBAL": "Group strategy", "EU": "Region Europe", "UK": "BMW UK", "CN": "BMW China", "US": "BMW of North America"}


def clean(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.replace("**", "")).strip()


def sources_of(md: str) -> dict[str, Source]:
    """'- **[S1] Label:** description. https://…' lines of the source register."""
    out = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r"^- \*\*\[(S\d+)\]\s*(.+?):?\*\*:?(.*)$", md, re.M):
        ref, label, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2).rstrip(":"), m.group(3)
        url = re.search(r"https?://\S+", rest)
        out[ref] = Source(ref=ref, label=clean(label), url=url.group(0).rstrip(".,)") if url else None)
    return out


def field(block: str, name: str) -> str | None:
    m = re.search(rf"\*\*{name}:\*\*\s*(.+?)(?=\n\s*\n|\Z)", block, re.S)
    return clean(m.group(1)) if m else None


def cited(text: str, register: dict[str, Source]) -> list[Source]:
    refs = dict.fromkeys(re.findall(r"\[(S\d+)\]", text))
    return [register[r] for r in refs if r in register]

        cls = re.search(r"\*\*Classification:\*\*\s*(.+?)\s*\*\*Confidence:\*\*\s*(\w+)", block)
        paras = [p for p in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", block.strip()) if p.strip() and not p.lstrip().startswith("**")]
        rows.append(Principle(
            id=pid, level="market", market=market, title=title,
            statement=field(block, "General principle") or clean(paras[0] if paras else title),
            evidence=clean(" ".join(paras)) or None, boundary=field(block, "Boundary"),

            sources=cited(block, register), owner=OWNERS[market],

    register = sources_of(md)

def series_principles(ts: str) -> list[Principle]:

                owner=p.group(3),
            ))
    return rows


def load_all() -> list[Principle]:
    rows = group_principles((L1 / "bmw_global_principles_across_four_markets.md").read_text())
    for market, name in MARKET_FILES.items():
        rows += market_principles(market, (L1 / name).read_text())
    return rows + series_principles(SERIES_TS.read_text())


async def main() -> None:

    by_level: dict[str, int] = {}
    for p in rows:
        by_level[p.market or p.series or ""] = by_level.get(p.market or p.series or "", 0) + 1
    print(f"parsed {len(rows)} principles:", by_level)
    if "--dry-run" in sys.argv:
        for p in rows[:3] + rows[-2:]:
            print(p.model_dump_json(indent=1)[:700])
        return
    store = make_store(get_settings())
    if not isinstance(store, SupabaseStore):
        sys.exit("Supabase is not configured (SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY in backend/.env)")
    print("upserted", await store.upsert_principles(rows))
    await store.aclose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

"""Principle assessor (L1): rates each feature request against BMW's principles for this series and market.

Inputs: the principles from Supabase (series fundamentals, market principles, Group principles), aggregate request data
(title, category, mention count, backing signal titles: no customer text) and, via a tool, the decision memory from
earlier generations. Output: a fit 0–1 per request with the principle ids it rests on, evidence and assumptions listed
separately, conflicts shown rather than averaged away. `verify` drops principle ids the agent was never given.
The fit replaces the series-focus fallback in the Dixi score's "principle fit" part (web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts).
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from pydantic_ai import Agent, RunContext
from pydantic_ai.models import Model

from app.db import Store
from app.models.assess import AssessRequest, AssessResult, AssessorOutput, RequestFit
from app.models.core import Principle
from app.models.signals import MARKET_NAMES, SERIES_NAMES
from app.scoring import build_memory

INSTRUCTIONS = """\
You are Dixi's principle assessor for BMW product managers. For every feature request, judge how well it fits the L1
principles you are given, in this order of weight: series fundamentals (they define the car), then market principles,
then Group principles. Principles are mostly about strategy, brand and market approach; say so when one only touches a
request indirectly instead of stretching it.

For each request return: fit (0 = conflicts, 0.5 = neutral / no principle speaks to it, 1 = strongly supported),
supports and tensions (principle ids only from the list), a rationale of at most 30 words, evidence (facts you used:
a principle's evidence, the mention count, a backing signal) and assumptions (anything you infer that the evidence
does not show). Never present an assumption as evidence. Respect each principle's boundary.

Call get_decision_memory once. If a request was rejected before, mention the reason and whether demand grew since
(state "resurfaced") in `memory`; do not lower the fit for it, the score applies memory separately.
conflicts: cases where strong customer demand meets a principle tension, or markets pull in different directions.
gaps: what the principles do not cover for this series and market. Assess every request id you are given."""


@dataclass
class AssessDeps:
    store: Store
    series: str
    market: str
    memory_calls: int = 0
    memory: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def build_assessor(model: Model | str) -> Agent[AssessDeps, AssessorOutput]:
    agent = Agent(model, name="principle_assessor", instructions=INSTRUCTIONS, deps_type=AssessDeps, output_type=AssessorOutput)

    @agent.tool
    async def get_decision_memory(ctx: RunContext[AssessDeps]) -> list[dict]:
        """Past keep/reject decisions on this series (and market) from earlier generations, with who, when and why."""
        ctx.deps.memory_calls += 1
        store = ctx.deps.store
        state = await store.get_settings()
        gens = [g.payload for g in await store.list_generations(ctx.deps.series)]
        mem = build_memory(gens, ctx.deps.series, ctx.deps.market, state.settings)
        ctx.deps.memory = mem
        return [{"title": k.split(":", 1)[1], "action": m.action, "reason": m.reason, "by": m.by, "at": m.at,
                 "mentionsAt": m.mentionsAt, "generation": m.generationId} for k, m in mem.items()]

    return agent


def principles_block(principles: list[Principle]) -> str:
    def line(p: Principle) -> str:
        bits = [f"[{p.id}] ({p.level}{'/' + p.market if p.market else ''}) {p.title}: {p.statement}"]
        if p.boundary:
            bits.append(f"  boundary: {p.boundary}")
        if p.evidence:
            bits.append(f"  evidence: {p.evidence[:400]}")
        if p.confidence:
            bits.append(f"  confidence: {p.confidence}")
        return "\n".join(bits)

    order = {"series": 0, "market": 1, "group": 2}
    return "\n".join(line(p) for p in sorted(principles, key=lambda p: (order[p.level], p.id)))


def prompt_for(req: AssessRequest, principles: list[Principle]) -> str:
    rows = "\n".join(
        f"- id={r.id} | {r.title} | {r.category} | {r.mentions} mentions"
        + (f" | backed by: {'; '.join(r.backing)}" if r.backing else "")
        for r in req.requests
    )
    return (
        f"Series: BMW {SERIES_NAMES[req.series]} ({req.series}). Market scope: {MARKET_NAMES.get(req.market, req.market)}.\n\n"
        f"L1 principles:\n{principles_block(principles)}\n\nFeature requests:\n{rows}"
    )


def verify(out: AssessorOutput, req: AssessRequest, principle_ids: set[str]) -> AssessorOutput:
    """Keep only known principle ids and known requests; report what was dropped or missing."""
    known_req = {r.id for r in req.requests}
    gaps = list(out.gaps)
    fits: list[RequestFit] = []
    for f in out.fits:
        if f.requestId not in known_req or any(x.requestId == f.requestId for x in fits):
            continue
        bad = [p for p in f.supports + f.tensions if p not in principle_ids]
        if bad:
            gaps.append(f"Dropped unknown principle ids {', '.join(sorted(set(bad)))} from \"{f.requestId}\".")
        fits.append(f.model_copy(update={"supports": [p for p in f.supports if p in principle_ids],
                                         "tensions": [p for p in f.tensions if p in principle_ids]}))
    missing = [r.title for r in req.requests if r.id not in {f.requestId for f in fits}]
    if missing:
        gaps.append(f"Not assessed (score keeps the series-focus fallback): {', '.join(missing)}.")
    return AssessorOutput(fits=fits, conflicts=out.conflicts, gaps=gaps)


async def run_assessment(agent: Agent[AssessDeps, AssessorOutput], store: Store, req: AssessRequest, model_label: str) -> AssessResult:
    from app.models.core import SCOPE_PRINCIPLE_MARKETS

    principles = await store.list_principles(SCOPE_PRINCIPLE_MARKETS[req.market], req.series)
    if not principles:
        raise LookupError("No L1 principles stored for this series and market (run scripts/seed_principles.py)")
    ids = {p.id for p in principles}
    deps = AssessDeps(store=store, series=req.series, market=req.market)
    result = await agent.run(prompt_for(req, principles), deps=deps)
    checked = verify(result.output, req, ids)
    out = AssessResult(**checked.model_dump(), series=req.series, market=req.market, principleIds=sorted(ids),
                       model=model_label, generatedAt=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"))
    out.id = await store.save_run("principle_assessments", {
        "series": req.series, "market": req.market, "principle_ids": sorted(ids),
        "request": req.model_dump(), "result": out.model_dump(exclude={"id"}), "model": model_label})
    return out

lines: +/* Dixi backend client (backend/, FastAPI). NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL turns on the server side:
+ * generations, decisions, scoring settings, L1 principles and agent runs are stored in Supabase through the API.
+ * Without it (e.g. a static demo) the app keeps everything in this browser (localStorage), as before.
+ * Every write goes to localStorage first and is then sent to the backend, so the UI never waits on the network.
+export async function api<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {
+  if (!API_URL) throw new Error("Backend not configured (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL).");
+    const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as { detail?: unknown } | null;
+    throw new Error(typeof body?.detail === "string" ? body.detail : `Backend error ${res.status} on ${path}`);
+  return (res.status === 204 ? null : await res.json()) as T;
+/* ---------- sync status (shown in the top bar) ---------- */
+export type SyncState = { mode: "local" | "synced" | "error"; at: string | null; error: string | null };
+let state: SyncState = { mode: API_URL ? "synced" : "local", at: null, error: null };
+/** Send a write to the backend; failures are shown in the top bar, the local copy stays. */
+export async function push(path: string, init: RequestInit): Promise<boolean> {
+    setState({ mode: "synced", at: new Date().toISOString(), error: null });
+    setState({ mode: "error", at: new Date().toISOString(), error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Sync failed" });
+/** Read from the backend; null when it is not configured or not reachable (callers keep the local copy). */
+export async function pull<T>(path: string): Promise<T | null> {
+    setState({ mode: "synced", at: new Date().toISOString(), error: null });
+    setState({ mode: "error", at: new Date().toISOString(), error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Backend unreachable" });

lines: +# Supabase: config + migrations (the CLI's .temp/ link state stays local)
# Entire (entire.io): shared settings, runners and agent hooks are committed; personal settings are not
+-- Dixi core schema: L1 principles, decisions (append-only history), generations, agent runs, scoring settings.
+-- Only the backend (secret key) reads and writes; RLS is on with no policies, so the public anon key gets nothing.
+-- BMW customer data (verbatims, quotes) is never stored here: requests are referenced by id + title only.
+-- L1 principles: Group-wide, per market (research in data/L1_Files) and per series (product fundamentals).
+  level          text not null check (level in ('group', 'market', 'series')),
+  statement      text not null,                    -- the principle itself
+  boundary       text,                             -- what it does not say / must not be inferred
+  classification text,                             -- explicit BMW principle · repeated practice · interpretation
+  confidence     text,                             -- High · Medium · Low (from the research)
+  sources        jsonb not null default '[]',      -- [{ref, label, url}]
+  owner          text not null,                    -- who may change it
+  active         boolean not null default true,
+  updated_at     timestamptz not null default now(),
+create index principles_market_idx on public.principles (market) where active;
+create index principles_series_idx on public.principles (series) where active;
+-- Every PM decision, append-only: an undo is its own row, so the history is never lost.
+  id            bigint generated always as identity primary key,
+  series        text not null check (series in ('F70', 'G60', 'G70')),
+  market        text not null,                     -- app scope: EU · US · CN · JP · ALL
+  request_id    text not null,                     -- feature request or signal id
+  action        text not null check (action in ('keep', 'reject', 'wish', 'undo')),
+  mentions_at   int,                               -- customer mentions at decision time (resurfacing rule)
+  at            timestamptz not null default now(),
+  generation_id text,                              -- set when the decision was saved with a build
+create index decisions_lookup_idx on public.decisions (series, market, request_id, at desc);
+-- Generations: every "Build profiles" (profiles, decisions, priority, social test) as the web app's Session object.
+  updated_at      timestamptz not null default now()
+create index generations_series_idx on public.generations (series, market, created_at desc);
+-- Agent runs, stored with their inputs and outputs so every signal and assessment can be traced.
+  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
+  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
+create index research_runs_idx on public.research_runs (series, market, created_at desc);
+  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
+  principle_ids   text[] not null,                 -- the principles the agent was given (snapshot of ids)
+  created_at      timestamptz not null default now()
+create index principle_assessments_idx on public.principle_assessments (series, market, created_at desc);
+-- Scoring settings (one row today; per-series rows later) and the log of every applied change.
+  updated_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
+  id          bigint generated always as identity primary key,
+  instruction text,                                -- the manager's words, if any
+  at          timestamptz not null default now()
+alter table public.principles            enable row level security;
+alter table public.decisions             enable row level security;
+alter table public.generations           enable row level security;
+alter table public.research_runs         enable row level security;
+alter table public.principle_assessments enable row level security;
+alter table public.scoring_settings      enable row level security;
+alter table public.scoring_changes       enable row level security;
+-- Evidence behind each principle (the documented facts it rests on), separate from the principle statement itself,
+-- so the agents can tell evidence from interpretation.
+alter table public.principles add column evidence text;

content.content:
Hear every market. Decide with a reason.

--- **Dixi** helps BMW product managers decide what the next car should offer. It listens to customers in every market, weighs what they say, and turns it into clear requirements. Every requirement keeps the reason it was chosen. *Named after the Dixi 3/15, BMW's first car (1928).* ## How Dixi thinks: three layers Not every input counts the same. Dixi sorts what it knows into three layers, from strongest to weakest. | | Layer | What goes in | How much it counts | |---|---|---|---| | 🟦 | **L1 · BMW principles** | The fundamentals of each series, owned by named managers. *Example: "The 7 Series puts rear-seat luxury first."* | Strongest. Every profile is checked against them. | | 🔵 | **L2 · Market evidence** | Customer feedback and feature requests, customer studies, sales, today's option list. A research agent adds competitor features people like and market trends, each with its sources. | The main engine. | | 🩵 | **L3 · Social test** | Runs only after profiles exist: which generated profile tracks better on social media (simulated for now). | Weakest, and set per series: 7 Series 2 %, 5 Series 8 %, 1 Series 20 %. | ## From customer voice to car profiles, in five steps 1. **Choose.** Pick a market on the globe, then a series (1, 5 or 7). 2. **Analyse.** AI reads the BMW principles and the market evidence, and builds one list of feature requests by category (Exterior, Interior, Digital, Powertrain) and urgency. 3. **Decide.** The product manager **keeps or rejects** each request (a reject always needs a reason), drags the list into priority order, and stars competitor features or trends onto a wishlist. Every decision records who and when. 4. **Build.** Dixi builds three car profiles (*Fix the basics*, *Tech-forward*, *Comfort & craft*) that follow the PM's priority. Each one exports as a catalogue-style PDF. 5. **Remember.** Each build is saved as a **generation** with its profiles, decisions and priority. Run the social test (L3) on it, or edit and rebuild. ```mermaid flowchart LR M[Market + series] --> A[AI analysis
L1 principles · L2 evidence
+ research agent] A --> H{{Product manager
keep · reject with reason
priority · wishlist}} H --> P[3 car profiles
follow the PM's priority] P --> G[(Generation
profiles · decisions · who · when)] G --> S[L3 social test
low weight] S -. "updates scores" .-> G G -. "edit and rebuild" .-> H ``` **Dixi is honest about what it doesn't know.** Missing markets, thin samples and conflicting signals are shown to the product manager, not hidden. ## Run it ```bash cd web pnpm install pnpm dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000, or see it live at **https://dixi-wheat.vercel.app**. Full setup (Supabase CLI, Vercel, Entire): [`docs/requirements.md`](docs/requirements.md). ## What's in the repo | Folder | What | |---|---| | [`web/`](web/) | The app: landing page with a live market globe, the requirement pipeline and the generations dashboard | | [`backend/`](backend/) | API and AI agents (planned) | | [`docs/`](docs/) | Setup, architecture diagrams, tech stack | | [`branding/`](branding/) | Logo, colours, brand guide | | [`scripts/`](scripts/) | Image generation, and the local data build for the pipeline | --- Built for the BMW challenge "AI for Product Decision Making" at the EHL Hackathon, Munich, October 2026. Dixi is a hackathon project and is not affiliated with BMW.

Hear every market. Decide with a reason.

--- **Dixi** helps BMW product managers decide what the next car should offer. It listens to customers in every market, weighs what they say, and turns it into clear requirements. Every requirement keeps the reason it was chosen. *Named after the Dixi 3/15, BMW's first car (1928).* ## How Dixi thinks: three layers Not every input counts the same. Dixi sorts what it knows into three layers, from strongest to weakest. | | Layer | What goes in | How much it counts | |---|---|---|---| | 🟦 | **L1 · BMW principles** | The fundamentals of each series, owned by named managers. *Example: "The 7 Series puts rear-seat luxury first."* | Strongest. Every profile is checked against them. | | 🔵 | **L2 · Market evidence** | Customer feedback and feature requests, customer studies, sales, today's option list. A research agent adds competitor features people like and market trends, each with its sources. | The main engine. | | 🩵 | **L3 · Social test** | Runs only after profiles exist: which generated profile tracks better on social media (simulated for now). | Weakest, and set per series: 7 Series 2 %, 5 Series 8 %, 1 Series 20 %. | ## From customer voice to car profiles, in five steps 1. **Choose.** Pick a market on the globe, then a series (1, 5 or 7). 2. **Analyse.** AI reads the BMW principles and the market evidence, and builds one list of feature requests by category (Exterior, Interior, Digital, Powertrain) and urgency. 3. **Decide.** The product manager **keeps or rejects** each request (a reject always needs a reason), drags the list into priority order, and stars competitor features or trends onto a wishlist. Every decision records who and when. 4. **Build.** Dixi builds three car profiles (*Fix the basics*, *Tech-forward*, *Comfort & craft*) that follow the PM's priority. Each one exports as a catalogue-style PDF. 5. **Remember.** Each build is saved as a **generation** with its profiles, decisions and priority. Run the social test (L3) on it, or edit and rebuild. ```mermaid flowchart LR M[Market + series] --> A[AI analysis
L1 principles · L2 evidence
+ research agent] A --> H{{Product manager
keep · reject with reason
priority · wishlist}} H --> P[3 car profiles
follow the PM's priority] P --> G[(Generation
profiles · decisions · who · when)] G --> S[L3 social test
low weight] S -. "updates scores" .-> G G -. "edit and rebuild" .-> H ``` **Dixi is honest about what it doesn't know.** Missing markets, thin samples and conflicting signals are shown to the product manager, not hidden. ## Run it ```bash cd web pnpm install pnpm dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000, or see it live at **https://dixi-wheat.vercel.app**. Full setup (Supabase CLI, Vercel, Entire): [`docs/requirements.md`](docs/requirements.md). ## What's in the repo | Folder | What | |---|---| | [`web/`](web/) | The app: landing page with a live market globe, the requirement pipeline and the generations dashboard | | [`backend/`](backend/) | API and AI agents (planned) | | [`docs/`](docs/) | Setup, architecture diagrams, tech stack | | [`branding/`](branding/) | Logo, colours, brand guide | | [`scripts/`](scripts/) | Image generation, and the local data build for the pipeline | --- Built for the BMW challenge "AI for Product Decision Making" at the EHL Hackathon, Munich, October 2026. ### Supabase
```bash
supabase login
supabase init                          # creates supabase/ (config + migrations)
supabase start                         # local Postgres + Studio; needs Docker running
supabase link --project-ref <project>  # connect to the hosted project
```

### Vercel (web hosting)

### Supabase
```bash
supabase login
supabase init                          # creates supabase/ (config + migrations)
supabase start                         # local Postgres + Studio; needs Docker running
supabase link --project-ref <project>  # connect to the hosted project
```

### Vercel (web hosting)

lines: The entities as built in `web/src/lib/pipeline/` (`types.ts`, `profiles.ts`, `sessions.ts`, `analytics.ts`, `series.ts`): series, markets, feature requests, option items, market signals, principles, decisions, generations, profiles, profile requirements and social-test campaigns.

-**Where it lives today.** Decisions and the priority order are stored per market + series in the browser (`localStorage`, keys `dixi:decisions:*` and `dixi:priority:*`); generations are stored there too (`dixi:sessions`, last 30). `by` and `created_by` come from a simple local "who is deciding" identity (`dixi:user`, `web/src/lib/user.ts`) until there is a login. Series, markets, feature requests, option items, studies and sales come from `web/data-local/pipeline.json`, built locally by `scripts/build-pipeline-data.py` and git-ignored; without it (e.g. on Vercel) the app uses example data with the same shape. Principles live in `series.ts` and market signals in `market-signals.ts` (example content and public sources). **Planned:** the same entities as Supabase tables, with a real login replacing the local identity.

+**Where it lives.** With the backend connected (`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`), these are **Supabase tables** (schema: `supabase/migrations/`), written and read only by the backend with its secret key (RLS on, no public policies):

+| `principles` | L1: Group (`GL-xx`), market (`EU-xx`, `UK-xx`, `CN-xx`, `US-xx`) and series (`G60-P1` …) principles with statement, evidence, boundary, classification, confidence, sources, owner, version | `backend/scripts/seed_principles.py`; owners via `PUT /principles/{id}` (version + 1) |

+| `decisions` | Every keep / reject / wish / **undo**, append-only, with who, role, when, reason, mentions at the time. A reject without a reason is refused by a check constraint | `POST /decisions` (web `decision-log.ts`) |
+| `generations` | Every build: the web app's `Session` (profiles, decisions, priority, social test, ids of the agent runs it used) | `PUT /generations/{id}` (web `sessions.ts`) |
