# Backend agents and storage, as built Status 11 Oct 2026, branch `backend-agents-tavily`. This page shows what the backend does today: two agents, the Supabase store and the decision memory that links generations. It also shows which data goes where and how this lines up with the design ([`01`](01-system-overview.md), [`05`](05-hitl-map.md), [`07`](07-pm-workflow.md), [`09`](09-scoring-and-memory.md)). Code: `backend/` (see its README), `supabase/migrations/`, and on the web side `web/src/lib/api.ts` and `web/src/lib/pipeline/{principles,research,decision-log,sessions}.ts`. **In one paragraph:** - **Feature requests:** BMW's data becomes feature requests locally, through a deterministic script. - **Principle assessor (L1):** during the analysis it rates every request against BMW principles stored in Supabase (series fundamentals, market principles, Group principles). It cites principle ids, keeps evidence and assumptions apart, and lists conflicts and gaps. Its fit is the score's *principle fit*. - **Research agent (L2):** the PM can start it. Two scouts search the web through Tavily; every source is checked against the real search results. - **The PM:** keeps, rejects (with a reason), orders and wishlists. - **Storage:** every decision, build, agent run and settings change is stored in Supabase. The next analysis rebuilds **decision memory** from the stored generations, so a past reject lowers that request's score until demand grows past the resurface threshold. ## 1. One analysis, step by step ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor PM as Product manager participant UI as Web · Pipeline
/dashboard/[market]/[series] participant API as FastAPI participant PA as principle_assessor
(strong OpenAI model) participant DB as Supabase PM->>UI: open Europe · 5 Series UI->>API: GET /principles?market=EU&series=G60 API->>DB: series G60-P1…P3 + EU-xx + UK-xx + GL-xx (30) UI->>API: POST /assess/principles
requests: id · title · category · mention count · backing titles API->>DB: principles for this scope API->>PA: principles (statement · boundary · evidence · confidence) + requests PA->>API: tool get_decision_memory() API->>DB: generations → build_memory (same rules as scoring.ts) API-->>PA: past keeps / rejects with reason, who, when, mentions then PA-->>API: per request: fit 0–1 · supports · tensions · rationale · evidence · assumptions · memory
+ conflicts + gaps API->>API: verify: drop principle ids it was not given, report unassessed requests API->>DB: principle_assessments (inputs + output + model) API-->>UI: assessment UI->>API: GET /generations · GET /decisions?series=G60&market=EU API->>DB: earlier builds · decision history UI->>UI: Dixi score = demand · backing · principle fit (assessor) → memory penalty / bonus UI-->>PM: ranked list · principles panel (conflicts, gaps) · "Rejected · reason · who" badges ``` A fresh browser reuses the stored assessment when the request set is the same (`GET /assess/principles/latest`, matched on `requestIds`), so the agent is not called twice for the same input. ## 2. Research agent (L2, started by the PM) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor PM as Product manager participant UI as Web · SignalsPanel participant API as POST /research/signals participant Lead as lead_researcher
(strong model) participant CS as competitor_scout
(fast model) participant TS as trend_scout
(fast model) participant TV as Tavily remote MCP
tavily_search · tavily_extract participant DB as Supabase PM->>UI: Run research agent UI->>API: series · market · feature-request titles (+ focus, categories) API->>Lead: prompt (no customer data) par Harness SubAgents · delegate_task Lead->>CS: competitors CS->>TV: ≤ 6 searches (soft budget, URLs recorded) CS-->>Lead: signals + gaps (JSON) and Lead->>TS: trends + regulation TS->>TV: ≤ 6 searches TS-->>Lead: signals + gaps (JSON) end Lead-->>API: merged · deduped · relatesTo linked to exact request titles · gaps API->>API: category filter · verify_sources (drop URLs Tavily never returned) API->>DB: research_runs API-->>UI: MarketSignal[] · gaps · searches UI->>UI: replaces the saved research for this market + series → backing, links, score, wishlist, profiles ``` - **Sources are checked by code, not by the model.** A signal left without a verified source is dropped and listed as a gap. - **Bounded cost.** At most about 12 Tavily credits per run (basic depth). Past its budget the search tool answers "budget used up, answer now" instead of aborting the run. - **One run, one decision trail.** The generation stores the id of the run (and of the assessment) it was built with. ## 3. Which data goes where ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef local fill:#fdecea,stroke:#e22718,color:#121722 classDef ours fill:#eef1f6,stroke:#5b6676,color:#121722 classDef ext fill:#e8f0fc,stroke:#1c69d4,color:#121722 subgraph LOCAL["This machine only (git-ignored)"] BMW[("data/ · BMW dataset
verbatims · studies · sales · options")]:::local L1F[("data/L1_Files
team research on BMW principles")]:::local SCR["scripts/build-pipeline-data.py
taxonomy → clusters, counts
no network, no LLM"]:::local PJ[("web/data-local/pipeline.json")]:::local end WEB["Web app
score · decisions · profiles"]:::ours API["FastAPI backend"]:::ours DB[("Supabase
principles · decisions · generations

# Backend agents and storage, as built Status 11 Oct 2026, branch `backend-agents-tavily`. This page shows what the backend does today: two agents, the Supabase store and the decision memory that links generations. It also shows which data goes where and how this lines up with the design ([`01`](01-system-overview.md), [`05`](05-hitl-map.md), [`07`](07-pm-workflow.md), [`09`](09-scoring-and-memory.md)). It cites principle ids, keeps evidence and assumptions apart, and lists conflicts and gaps. Its fit is the score's *principle fit*. - **Research agent (L2):** the PM can start it. Two scouts search the web through Tavily; every source is checked against the real search results. - **The PM:** keeps, rejects (with a reason), orders and wishlists. - **Storage:** every decision, build, agent run and settings change is stored in Supabase. The next analysis rebuilds **decision memory** from the stored generations, so a past reject lowers that request's score until demand grows past the resurface threshold. ## 1. /dashboard/[market]/[series] participant API as FastAPI participant PA as principle_assessor

(strong model) participant CS as competitor_scout
(fast model) participant TS as trend_scout

lines: - **Challenge:** derive, justify and prioritise customer requirements for a BMW successor vehicle (1/5/7 Series; Europe, China, USA; 3–5 years ahead). The product manager stays in control, every decision is traceable, evidence and assumptions stay separate, and conflicts are shown, not averaged away.

- **Judging rubric:** decision and scoring logic · workflow and human decisions · traceability and auditability (incl. postponements) · quality, usability and feasibility · innovation, scale and business impact · plus "we reward honesty" (surface missing evidence, conflicts and uncertainty). Logic, workflow and traceability come first when deciding what to build.

-- **Product: Dixi**, named after the Dixi 3/15, BMW's first car (1928). A principled, weighted, traceable requirement engine: three layers (L1 principles, L2 evidence, L3 signals), source weights per model, human gates G1–G4, an editable decision memory, lineage from comment to requirement, and "what we don't know" gap cards. Architecture: `docs/architecture/`.

+- **Product: Dixi**, named after the Dixi 3/15, BMW's first car (1928). A principled, weighted, traceable requirement engine: three layers (L1 principles, L2 evidence, L3 social test). **Built:** principle assessor (L1, principles in Supabase), research agent (L2, Tavily), Dixi score with decision memory across generations, PM gate (keep / reject with reason / priority / wishlist), 3 profiles, append-only decision history. **Target design, not built:** gates G1–G4, Codebeamer export, postpone, lineage store, per-model source weights. Keep README and docs honest about this split. As built: `docs/architecture/10-backend-agents.md`; design: `docs/architecture/`.

- **Mandatory:** the repo must use **Entire** (entire.io): `entire enable --agent claude-code`, connect the repo on entire.io, turn on Runners and Trails. Submissions without Entire are rejected. Agent transcripts are uploaded on push (and are public if the repo is public): never paste secrets into a session. Work goes through trails (§5).

Shared globe: `web/src/components/globe/MarketGlobe.tsx`. Data modules: `web/src/lib/markets.ts`, `web/src/lib/dashboard-data.ts` (example data, no real BMW data) |

Inputs sit in three layers: **L1 BMW principles** (the fundamentals of each series, owned by managers), **L2 market evidence** (customer feedback and feature requests, customer studies, sales, today's option list, plus a research agent that adds competitor features people like and market trends, each with sources) and **L3 social test** (runs only after profiles exist: which profile tracks better on social media; low weight per series: 7 Series 2 %, 5 Series 8 %, 1 Series 20 %). The PM picks a market and a series; AI clusters the evidence into feature requests by category and urgency; the PM keeps or rejects each one (a reject needs a reason), drags them into priority order and wishlists competitor or trend features. Dixi then builds three profiles that follow that priority (score = L1 principles + priority fit, plus L2 coverage) and saves the build as a **generation** with its profiles, decisions and priority. Every decision records who made it (name and role, from a simple local identity until there is a login) and when, and shows up in the decision log, the profile's decision trail and its PDF. Today decisions, priority and generations live in the browser (localStorage); BMW-derived data stays local and git-ignored, and the public deployment runs on example data. Every build is stored as a generation. `build_memory` (Python) and `buildMemory` (web) take the latest keep or reject per request from earlier generations of the same series (and market, unless the team set memory scope to "all"). A past reject lowers the score with a half-life, and lifts once demand has grown past the team's resurface threshold. A past keep adds a small bonus. The principle assessor reads the same memory through its tool. Matching is by series and request title today; pgvector similarity for reworded requests is planned.

## Core ideas in one paragraph
Dixi helps a BMW product manager turn what each market says into car profiles for the next 1, 5 or 7 Series, and keeps the reason for every decision. Inputs sit in three layers: **L1 BMW principles** (the fundamentals of each series, owned by managers), **L2 market evidence** (customer feedback and feature requests, customer studies, sales, today's option list, plus a research agent that adds competitor features people like and market trends, each with sources) and **L3 social test** (runs only after profiles exist: which profile tracks better on social media; low weight per series: 7 Series 2 %, 5 Series 8 %, 1 Series 20 %). The PM picks a market and a series; AI clusters the evidence into feature requests by category and urgency; the PM keeps or rejects each one (a reject needs a reason), drags them into priority order and wishlists competitor or trend features. Dixi then builds three profiles that follow that priority (score = L1 principles + priority fit, plus L2 coverage) and saves the build as a **generation** with its profiles, decisions and priority. Every decision records who made it (name and role, from a simple local identity until there is a login) and when, and shows up in the decision log, the profile's decision trail and its PDF. Today decisions, priority and generations live in the browser (localStorage); BMW-derived data stays local and git-ignored, and the public deployment runs on example data. Supabase tables are planned.

See also: [`tech-stack/`](tech-stack/README.md) (technology choices, versions, alternatives) and `../backend/` (FastAPI API: principle assessor, research agent, Supabase store).

content.text:
The whole flow you described now works end to end, and I checked it in the browser against the hosted Supabase project. The README and docs only claim what the code does. The social test (your Instagram analysis) is still simulated and labelled as such.

**What works now**
- **BMW data:** a local script turns it into feature requests with mention counts per market; no AI, no network. The analysis screen says so on each step instead of claiming "AI clusters".
- **Your L1 principle research is in Supabase:** 53 principles from `data/L1_Files` plus `series.ts`. That's 10 BMW Group, 9 Europe, 8 UK, 9 China and 8 USA principles, plus 3 per series. Each one keeps its evidence, boundary, confidence and sources; the raw files stay local.
- **New AI step, the principle assessor:**
  - It runs during the analysis and rates every request against that market's principles (Europe includes the UK).
  - For each request it gives a 0–1 fit, cites principle IDs, and lists evidence and assumptions separately.
  - It lists conflicts instead of averaging them, and reads past decisions through a tool.
  - Its fit is the "principle fit" part of the score, and it drives each profile's principle score.
- **Competitors and trends:** the research agent from before, now saving every run to Supabase.
- **Decisions and memory:** every keep, reject and undo is stored in Supabase with who, when and why, and a reject without a reason is refused. Builds and settings changes are stored too, and the next analysis rebuilds decision memory from Supabase.
- **Scoring formula:** the same in the web app and the backend; tests pin both to the same numbers.

**Verified in the browser (Europe, 5 Series):**
1. The assessor rated 20 requests against 30 principles.
2. I kept 3, rejected one with a reason, and built the profiles.
3. In a cleared browser everything came back from Supabase:
   - the kept requests showed "Kept before" with their bonus;
   - the rejected one showed the reason and the person who rejected it, and dropped to a score of 10 and last place;
   - a second cleared browser reused the stored assessment instead of calling the AI again.

With the backend switched off, the app still works on local data and the top bar shows "Not saved".

**Problems found and fixed.** Two independent subagent audits checked the repo the way a judge would. The serious finding was that **BMW customer quotes had been uploaded to Supabase** inside a saved build. I stripped them on both the web and backend sides, with a test, and removed the 27 quotes already stored. Supabase's point-in-time backups may still hold the old row for a while. The other fixes:
- Every decision was being written twice.
- Deleted builds came back after a sync.
- The stored assessment wasn't redone after new research.
- Several claims in the UI and docs weren't true: "compare generations", "tune per model", "AI clusters", "every priority change logged", and a contact form that said "sent" but sent nothing.

Gates G1–G4, the Codebeamer export and postponing are now clearly marked as target design.

All 23 backend tests pass, and the web app passes type-check, lint and a production build. The work is in 13 commits on `backend-agents-tavily`, all pushed.

**What you need to do:**
- **Deploy the backend:** run `! cd backend && uv run fastapi login`, then I can deploy. The README's secrets step now includes the Supabase keys. After that, `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` needs setting on Vercel, which I'll only do once you OK it.
- **Supabase key:** the CLI only shows the new secret key masked, so the backend uses the legacy `service_role` key. Paste the real secret key from the dashboard if you'd rather use the new key type.
- **Demo data:** Supabase now holds my test build (Marco Rossi, 3 keeps and 1 reject). It's useful for demoing memory; say if you want it deleted.
- **Contact address:** the contact form now links to `team@dixi.dev` (it was already in the footer). Confirm it's a real address.
- **Merge:** open and merge the trail and PR on entire.io.

Yes, these are real customer comments from the BMW dataset. Nothing in them is written or generated by AI.

**Where they come from:**
- **Source file:** the "Customer Feedback" column of `data/bmw/feedback/<series>_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`, sheet "Feedback_Explorer" (`scripts/build-pipeline-data.py:527`).
- **How they're chosen:** the data build script (`pick_quotes`, line 588) takes up to 3 comments per feature request from the rows behind that request. It prefers "wants" over "difficult to use" over "defects", picks comments of roughly 130 characters, and spreads them across markets. It's a fixed rule, not AI, and the text is only cleaned up, not rewritten.
- **Where they're stored:** in `web/data-local/pipeline.json`, which only exists on your machine.

I checked that the first quote in your screenshot is in that file and appears in no tracked file in git.

**Where they show up:**
- **Locally:** they appear in the request details ("Customers say") when the app runs on your machine.
- **On the public site (Vercel):** this section is empty, because the example data has no quotes.
- **Never sent elsewhere:** they don't go to OpenAI or Tavily. Since the fix in the last round they don't go to Supabase either.

One thing to watch: this session's transcript now contains customer quotes, from your screenshot and from my check, which searched for a phrase of the first quote. Agent transcripts are uploaded to Entire on the next push. content.text:
It depends on which screen you mean. When you pick a series, the analysis runs one real AI call. The **Analytics** tab (the social test) is not AI at all; it's simulated.

**When you pick a series (the analysis screen):**

| Step on screen | What happens | AI? |
|---|---|---|
| Loading BMW principles | Real request to the backend, which reads them from Supabase | No, database |
| Reading customer comments, studies, sales, options | Shows data the script prepared earlier (`pipeline.json`); nothing is computed at that moment | No, prepared in advance |
| Competitors & trends | Shows the saved research or the last live run; it doesn't search at this step | No (the research agent only runs when you click **Run research agent**) |
| Linking requests, scoring urgency | Rules in the code | No |
| **Principle assessor** | Real call to OpenAI through the backend, about 50 s. If the same requests were already assessed, it reuses the stored result instead | **Yes** |

Without the backend connected, the last step reads "Principle fit: series focus only" and no AI runs.

**The Analytics tab (social test, L3):** nothing is posted and no AI runs. **Launch test (simulated)** generates 14 days of engagement curves from a seeded random generator (`simulateCampaigns` in `web/src/lib/pipeline/analytics.ts`). The seed is market + series + generation, so the same build always gives the same curves. Those numbers then nudge the profile scores by the small L3 weight (2 % for the 7 Series, 8 % for the 5 Series, 20 % for the 1 Series). The UI labels it "simulated". This is the part you said is fine to leave out, because real social data needs integrations.

| **BMW principles** | The **principle assessor** really runs (OpenAI, about 50 s) and rates every request against the principles, unless the same requests were already assessed. | ✅ Live AI |

So "it analyses everything after you select" is only true for the principles. For the other two it shows earlier results.

I can make the analysis step do all three live:
1. **Auto-run the research agent during the analysis**, only when no stored run exists for that market and car. The first time takes about a minute and roughly 12 credits; after that it reuses the stored run from Supabase. This keeps credit use low.
2. **Add an "evidence analyst" agent for the BMW data** that runs at that step. It would read the request counts, the feedback types (wants, hard to use, defects), the customer-study scores and the sales volumes for that market. It would return the main findings, thin samples, and cases where demand and sales disagree, with evidence and assumptions kept separate. It uses aggregate numbers only, so no customer comments go to OpenAI.
3. Optional and not recommended without BMW's OK: have AI group the raw customer comments itself. That would send BMW customer text to OpenAI.

I'd do 1 and 2. That makes "Dixi analyses trends, competitors and BMW data when you pick a car" literally true, and keeps the data rules. Should I go ahead?

Here's the table, built from the code and the end-to-end browser test. The rows are the claims in the README, docs and UI.

| # | What we say | What the code actually does | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dixi analyses **BMW data** for the chosen market and series | `scripts/build-pipeline-data.py` maps BMW's feedback taxonomy to feature requests and counts mentions per market and type, plus studies, sales and options. It's **run by hand beforehand** and rule-based, with no AI. The screen loads the result (`pipeline.json`, local only) | ✅ True, as documented: prepared in advance, not AI |
| 2 | **Competitors and trends** with sources | The research agent (a lead plus 2 scouts on Tavily MCP) works, and code drops any source Tavily didn't return. It runs **only when the PM clicks**. Otherwise the screen shows the last stored run or the saved research from 10 Oct (written in an earlier session and curated, not a backend run) | ✅ Agent real, on demand; ⚠️ the default view is earlier research |
| 3 | **L1 principles** per series and market, in Supabase | 53 principles seeded from your L1 files and `series.ts`, and served per scope (Europe includes the UK) | ✅ |
| 4 | **AI checks every request against the principles** | The principle assessor runs **live** in the analysis step: fit, cited IDs, evidence vs assumptions, conflicts, gaps. Unknown IDs are dropped, and the run is stored | ✅ Live AI (the only AI that runs on selection) |
| 5 | **Dixi score** = demand · backing · principle fit + decision memory | `scoring.ts`, with a Python copy pinned by tests. Principle fit comes from the assessor, with the series focus as fallback | ✅ |
| 6 | Weights set in Settings, by sliders or in plain words, every change logged | Works; the plain-words AI proposes and the manager applies. Logged in Supabase with who, source and before → after. **The same settings apply to every series** | ✅ (not per series) |
| 7 | PM keeps or rejects (reason required), sets priority, wishlists | Works. A reject without a reason is blocked in the UI, the API and the database. Decisions are append-only in Supabase | ✅ |
| 8 | Every decision records **who** and **when** | Recorded, but "who" is a **local preset user** (e.g. Marco Rossi) with no login. **Priority moves are not logged** individually; only the final order is saved | ⚠️ Partly |
| 9 | Builds saved as **generations**; the next generation remembers | Stored in Supabase. The next analysis rebuilds memory: rejects drop with their reason shown, keeps get a bonus, a reject resurfaces when demand grows ≥ 30 %. Verified in a cleared browser | ✅ |
| 10 | Memory recognises the same request again | Matches on **series + exact title**. Reworded requests are not recognised (pgvector is planned) | ⚠️ Exact match only |
| 11 | **3 car profiles** following the PM's priority, with principle fit | Built by **fixed rules** (3 archetypes), not by AI. L1 = 70 % principle fit + 30 % priority. Tensions with principles are listed | ✅ Rule-based, not AI |
| 12 | Profile PDF | The browser's print dialog | ✅ (print, not a generated PDF) |
| 13 | **Social test (L3)** | **Simulated**: seeded random curves, nothing is posted, labelled "simulated" | 🟡 Simulated (agreed) |
| 14 | Honest about gaps and conflicts | Both agents return gaps, the assessor lists conflicts, and markets without comments fall back to all markets with a warning. The analysis screen names each step's data source | ✅ |
| 15 | BMW customer text never leaves the machine | Quotes stay local. OpenAI gets titles, categories and counts. Supabase gets no quotes since the fix; the old row is cleaned, but backups may still hold it. ⚠️ This session's transcript contains quotes and goes to Entire on push | ✅ in code; ⚠️ transcript |
| 16 | Monthly refresh of feedback and trends | **Not built**, documented as planned (cron) | ⚪ Planned |
| 17 | Gates G1–G4, engineering check, Codebeamer export, postpone, comparing generations, lineage store | **Not built**, marked as target design | ⚪ Planned |
| 18 | Live at **dixi-wheat.vercel.app** | The live site has **no backend**: it runs on example data, keeps everything in the browser, has no principle assessor or research agent, and its analysis step says "series focus only". Everything in rows 2–10 that involves the backend works **only locally** until the backend is deployed and `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is set on Vercel | ⚠️ The biggest gap a judge will hit |

message.content: how would you score this project? base on facts

content.text:
I'd score it about **7 out of 10** today. It would be roughly **7.8** once the backend is live on the public site. Below, each criterion of the hackathon's judging rubric is scored 1–10 from the code and the end-to-end test; the weighting by rubric priority is my own choice.

| Criterion (rubric order) | Score | Why, based on facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision and scoring logic** | **8** | **For:** a clear, published formula (demand · backing · principle fit), with decision memory (half-life decay, resurfacing at +30 % demand, keep bonus). The same logic exists in TypeScript and Python, pinned by tests. Principle fit comes from an AI assessor that cites principle IDs, and unknown IDs are dropped by code. **Against:** request grouping is rule-based, not learned. Memory matches exact titles only. Settings are global, not per series. Assessor fits run high (most were 0.65–0.98 in the test), so the principle part separates requests weakly. |
| **Workflow and human decisions** | **7.5** | **For:** the PM really controls the outcome. Keep or reject with a required reason (enforced in the UI, the API and the database), drag priority (which overrides the score), wishlist, edit and rebuild. The AI only proposes: the assessor, the research agent, the plain-words settings. **Against:** gates G1–G4, postpone and the engineering check are design only. Research is manual. The 3 profiles come from fixed rules, so with few kept requests all three are identical (seen in the test). |
| **Traceability and auditability (incl. postponements)** | **7** | **For:** append-only decision history with who, when and why, where an undo is its own row. Every agent run is stored with inputs, output and model, and a generation links to the runs it used. Sources are verified against search results. There's a settings change log, and the trace popup per requirement. Entire records why each line of code exists. **Against:** postponement doesn't exist, and that's named in the rubric. Priority moves aren't logged individually. "Who" is a preset user with no login. There's no lineage view from comment to requirement. |
| **Quality, usability and feasibility** | **7** | **For:** a polished UI, 23 offline backend tests, type-check, lint and a production build all passing. It works without the backend, and is honest when the backend is down. The stack is realistic (FastAPI, Supabase, Tavily) at low cost (about 12 credits per research run). **Against:** the public site runs without the backend, so judges clicking the live link see none of the agents or the Supabase storage. There are no web tests. It was built fast, and two audits found real bugs, including the quote leak (now fixed). |
| **Innovation, scale and business impact** | **6.5** | **For:** principles kept as data, which the AI must cite. Evidence and assumptions are kept apart. Conflicts are shown, not averaged. Memory carries across generations so rejected ideas don't keep coming back. The planned monthly refresh is a credible path to scale. **Against:** the cron job, a real social test, pgvector and the Codebeamer hand-off aren't built. There's no measured impact, such as time saved or decision quality. The agent architecture itself (orchestrator plus sub-agents) is a known pattern. |
| **Honesty** ("we reward honesty") | **8.5** | **For:** every agent returns gaps. The analysis screen names each step's real source. The README has a "what works / planned" table with code links. Simulated parts are labelled. False claims were actively removed (compare, per-model weights, "AI clusters", a fake contact form). **Against:** the default research view is curated research from 10 Oct, labelled "Saved research" but easy to mistake for a live run. And the incident: quotes reached Supabase until the audit caught it. |

**Overall:**
- **About 7.3 by my weighting.** I weighted the three criteria the rubric puts first a bit higher: scoring logic 25 %, workflow 20 %, traceability 20 %, the other three 35 % together.
- **Best case: about 7.8** once the backend is deployed and the live site uses it.
- **Worst case: about 6** if a judge only clicks the public site and sees example data with no agents.

**Highest-impact fixes, ranked by points gained per hour:**
1. **Deploy the backend and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` on Vercel.** This turns most of the work into something judges can see; probably +0.5 to +1.
2. **Add "Postpone" as a third decision** (with reason and revisit date, stored like a reject). It's named in the rubric and fits the existing append-only decisions table; about 2 hours. *(inferred)*
3. **Run research automatically when no stored run exists**, so a judge's first analysis shows live, sourced trends.
4. **Make the profiles differ** when few requests are kept, or say why they're identical.
5. **Log priority moves** as decisions, so "every change has who and when" is fully true.

"""Generation chat: a PM asks questions about one generation; answers come only from retrieved facts."""
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class ChatTurn(BaseModel):
    role: Literal["user", "assistant"]
    content: str = Field(max_length=4000)


class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    generationId: str
    question: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=1000)
    profileId: str | None = Field(default=None, description="The profile the PM is looking at, if any")
    history: list[ChatTurn] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=12)


class ChatOutput(BaseModel):
    answer: str = Field(description="Plain English, short. Only facts from the tools; say clearly what is not in them")
    cited: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Fact ids used: principle ids, request titles, decision dates, run ids")


class ChatResponse(ChatOutput):
    sources: list[str] = Field(description="What was actually retrieved for this answer (recorded by code, not the model)")
    model: str

Use the tools to look things up; never answer from general knowledge about BMW or cars. Call get_generation first.
Rules:
- Only state facts the tools returned. If the answer is not in them, say so plainly ("This generation does not record …").
- Name your evidence: request titles, principle ids (e.g. EU-03, G60-P1), decision who/when/reason, signal titles.
- Keep evidence and assumptions apart; label anything inferred as "inferred".
- The social test (L3) is simulated; say so when you use it.
- Short answers: a few sentences or a short list. Put the ids you used in `cited`."""


@dataclass
class ChatDeps:
    store: Store
    generation: Generation
    sources: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def note(self, s: str) -> None:
        if s not in self.sources:
            self.sources.append(s)


def _profiles(p: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    out = []
    for pr in p.get("profiles", []):
        s = pr.get("score", {})
        out.append({
            "id": pr.get("id"), "name": pr.get("name"), "tagline": pr.get("tagline"),
            "score": {k: round(v, 3) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in s.items()},
            "requirements": [{"priority": r.get("priority"), "title": r.get("title"), "category": r.get("category"),
                              "mentions_in_market": r.get("scoped"), "summary": r.get("summary")} for r in pr.get("requests", [])],
            "wishlist": [w.get("title") for w in pr.get("wishes", [])],
            "backing_signals": [{"title": b.get("title"), "kind": b.get("kind"), "competitor": b.get("competitor"),
                                 "detail": b.get("detail"), "sources": [x.get("url") for x in b.get("sources", [])]}
                                for b in pr.get("backing", [])],
            "why": pr.get("why", []),
            "principles": pr.get("principles"),
        })
    return out


def build_chat_agent(model: Model | str) -> Agent[ChatDeps, ChatOutput]:
    agent = Agent(model, name="generation_analyst", instructions=INSTRUCTIONS, deps_type=ChatDeps, output_type=ChatOutput)

    @agent.tool
    async def get_generation(ctx: RunContext[ChatDeps]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The generation: who built it and when, the 3 profiles (scores, requirements in PM priority, wishlist,
        backing signals, why, principle tensions), every decision with reason, the social test if run."""
        g = ctx.deps.generation
        p = g.payload
        ctx.deps.note(f"generation {g.id}")
        decisions = sorted((p.get("decisions") or {}).values(), key=lambda d: d.get("at", ""))
        return {
            "id": g.id, "series": g.series, "series_name": p.get("seriesName"), "market": p.get("scopeLabel", g.market),
            "built_by": g.createdBy, "built_by_role": g.createdByRole, "built_at": g.createdAt,
            "profiles": _profiles(p),
            "decisions": [{"title": d.get("title"), "action": d.get("action"), "reason": d.get("reason"), "by": d.get("by"),
                           "role": d.get("role"), "at": d.get("at"), "mentions_at_decision": d.get("mentionsAt")} for d in decisions],
            "social_test": ("simulated; " + ", ".join(f"{c.get('profileId')}: L3 {round(c.get('l3', 0), 2)}" for c in p["campaigns"]))

            "agent_runs": {"assessment": p.get("assessmentId"), "research": p.get("researchRunId")},

    async def get_principles(ctx: RunContext[ChatDeps], ids: list[str] | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:

        rows = await ctx.deps.store.list_principles(SCOPE_PRINCIPLE_MARKETS.get(g.market, ["GLOBAL"]), g.series)

        return [{"id": p.id, "level": p.level, "title": p.title, "statement": p.statement, "boundary": p.boundary,

    async def get_assessment(ctx: RunContext[ChatDeps]) -> dict[str, Any]:

        g = ctx.deps.generation
        rid = g.payload.get("assessmentId")
        row = (await ctx.deps.store.get_run("principle_assessments", rid)) if rid else None
        row = row or await ctx.deps.store.latest_run("principle_assessments", g.series, g.market)
        if not row:
            return {"note": "No principle assessment is stored for this generation."}
        ctx.deps.note(f"principle assessment {row['id']}" + ("" if rid == row["id"] else " (latest, not linked to this build)"))
        titles = {r["id"]: r["title"] for r in row.get("request", {}).get("requests", [])}
        res = row["result"]
        return {
            "assessed_at": res.get("generatedAt"), "model": res.get("model"),
            "fits": [{"request": titles.get(f["requestId"], f["requestId"]), "fit": f["fit"], "supports": f["supports"],
                      "tensions": f["tensions"], "rationale": f["rationale"], "evidence": f["evidence"],
                      "assumptions": f["assumptions"], "memory": f.get("memory")} for f in res.get("fits", [])],
            "conflicts": res.get("conflicts", []), "gaps": res.get("gaps", []),
        }

    @agent.tool
    async def get_research(ctx: RunContext[ChatDeps]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The live research run (competitors and trends) this build used, or the latest for its series + market."""
        g = ctx.deps.generation
        rid = g.payload.get("researchRunId")
        row = (await ctx.deps.store.get_run("research_runs", rid)) if rid else None
        row = row or await ctx.deps.store.latest_run("research_runs", g.series, g.market)

        res = row["result"]
        return {"run_at": res.get("generatedAt"), "searches": res.get("searches"),
                "signals": [{"title": s["title"], "kind": s["kind"], "competitor": s.get("competitor"), "detail": s["detail"],
                             "strength": s["strength"], "relates_to": s.get("relatesTo", []),
                             "sources": [x["url"] for x in s.get("sources", [])]} for s in res.get("signals", [])],
                "gaps": res.get("gaps", [])}

    async def get_decision_memory(ctx: RunContext[ChatDeps]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Decision memory for this series + market across all generations: latest keep/reject per request."""
        g = ctx.deps.generation
        state = await ctx.deps.store.get_settings()
        gens = [x.payload for x in await ctx.deps.store.list_generations(g.series)]
        mem = build_memory(gens, g.series, g.market, state.settings)
        ctx.deps.note(f"decision memory ({len(mem)} requests, {g.series} · {g.market})")
        return [{"request": k.split(":", 1)[1], "action": m.action, "reason": m.reason, "by": m.by, "at": m.at,
                 "generation": m.generationId} for k, m in mem.items()]

    return agent


def prompt_for(req: ChatRequest) -> str:
    lines = []
    if req.history:
        lines.append("Conversation so far:")
        lines += [f"{t.role}: {t.content}" for t in req.history[-8:]]
        lines.append("")
    if req.profileId:
        lines.append(f"The PM is looking at profile '{req.profileId}'.")
    lines.append(f"Question: {req.question}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

import json

from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelMessage, ModelResponse, ToolCallPart, ToolReturnPart
from pydantic_ai.models.function import AgentInfo, FunctionModel

from app.agents.chat import build_chat_agent
from app.models.core import Generation, Principle

    "id": "G-1", "series": "G60", "scope": "EU", "scopeLabel": "Europe", "seriesName": "5 Series",

    "profiles": [{"id": "fix", "name": "Fix the basics", "score": {"l1": 0.8, "l2": 0.6, "l3": None, "total": 0.7},
                  "requests": [{"title": "More real-world electric range", "category": "Powertrain", "priority": 1, "scoped": 13, "quotes": []}],
                  "wishes": [], "backing": [], "why": ["Covers 13 customer mentions."], "principles": None}],
    "decisions": {"r9": {"requestId": "r9", "title": "More storage and luggage space", "action": "reject",
                         "reason": "Boot space is fixed by the platform", "by": "Marco Rossi", "at": "2026-10-11T09:05:00Z"}},
    "campaigns": None, "assessmentId": None, "researchRunId": None,
}


def test_chat_answers_from_retrieved_facts_and_lists_sources():
    seen: dict = {}

    def model(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
        returns = [p for m in messages for p in getattr(m, "parts", []) if isinstance(p, ToolReturnPart)]
        if not returns:
            return ModelResponse(parts=[ToolCallPart("get_generation", {}), ToolCallPart("get_principles", {"ids": ["G60-P1"]})])
        gen = next(r for r in returns if r.tool_name == "get_generation").content
        seen["decision"] = gen["decisions"][0]
        out = {"answer": f"It was rejected by {gen['decisions'][0]['by']}: {gen['decisions'][0]['reason']}.",
               "cited": ["More storage and luggage space", "G60-P1"]}
        return ModelResponse(parts=[ToolCallPart(info.output_tools[0].name, out)])

    from app.main import app

    with TestClient(app) as c:
        store = app.state.store
        store.principles = {"G60-P1": Principle(id="G60-P1", level="series", series="G60", title="Comfort first",
                                                 statement="Business sedan first.", owner="PM 5 Series")}
        store.generations["G-1"] = Generation(id="G-1", series="G60", market="EU", createdAt=PAYLOAD["createdAt"],
                                              createdBy="Marco Rossi", payload=PAYLOAD)
        app.state.chat_agent = build_chat_agent(FunctionModel(model))
        r = c.post("/chat/generation", json={"generationId": "G-1", "question": "Why was luggage space rejected?", "profileId": "fix"})
        assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
        body = r.json()
        assert "Boot space is fixed" in body["answer"]
        assert body["sources"] == ["generation G-1", "principles G60-P1"]
        assert seen["decision"]["by"] == "Marco Rossi"
        assert "quotes" not in json.dumps(seen)  # the chat never sees customer text

        assert c.post("/chat/generation", json={"generationId": "G-missing", "question": "?"}).status_code == 404
EOF

lines: - **Feature requests:** BMW's data becomes feature requests locally, through a deterministic script.
+- **Generation chat:** on a profile page the PM can ask about that build, and an agent answers from facts it looks up (§2b).

- **Principle assessor (L1):** during the analysis it rates every request against BMW principles stored in Supabase (series fundamentals, market principles, Group principles). It cites principle ids, keeps evidence and assumptions apart, and lists conflicts and gaps. Its fit is the score's *principle fit*.
- **Research agent (L2):** the PM can start it. Two scouts search the web through Tavily; every source is checked against the real search results.
- **The PM:** keeps, rejects (with a reason), orders and wishlists.
- **Bounded cost.** At most about 12 Tavily credits per run (basic depth). Past its budget the search tool answers "budget used up, answer now" instead of aborting the run.
- **One run, one decision trail.** The generation stores the id of the run (and of the assessment) it was built with.
+## 2b. Generation chat: ask about one build

+On every profile page the PM can ask questions about that generation ("Why was luggage space rejected?", "Which principles does this profile strain?"). A small agent, `generation_analyst` (fast model), answers **only from facts it looks up with tools**; it has no general knowledge to fall back on by instruction, and says when something is not recorded.

+FastAPI API with three AI agents and the store behind the dashboard:

- **Principle assessor (L1):** rates each feature request against BMW principles stored in Supabase. It returns a fit per request with cited principle ids, evidence and assumptions kept separate, conflicts and gaps. Its fit is the *principle fit* in the Dixi score.
- **Research agent (L2):** competitor features customers like and market trends, every one with traced sources.
+- **Generation chat:** answers a PM's questions about one generation from facts it retrieves with tools, and lists what it looked up.
- **Store (Supabase):** principles, decisions (append-only), generations, agent runs, scoring settings with a change log, and the decision memory that the next generation reads.
The web app (`web/`) uses all of it when `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is set. Without it, the web app falls back to the browser and the saved research.

| `PUT /generations/{id}` · `GET /generations` · `DELETE /generations/{id}` | Saved builds (the web app's Session object) |
| `GET /memory?series&market` | Decision memory as the next generation sees it (`app/scoring.py`, same rules as `web/src/lib/pipeline/scoring.ts`) |
- **`verify`** drops principle ids the agent was not given, de-duplicates, and lists requests it did not assess as gaps. The score then keeps the series-focus fallback for those requests.

- **Seed:** `uv run python -I scripts/seed_principles.py` parses the team's L1 research in `../data/L1_Files` (local, git-ignored) and the series fundamentals in `web/src/lib/pipeline/series.ts`, then upserts 53 rows. `--dry-run` prints them.
+`generation_analyst` (fast model) answers a PM's question about one generation. Its tools:
+- `get_generation`: profiles, requirements in priority, decisions with reasons, wishlist, backing signals, social test.
+- `get_assessment` and `get_research`: the runs this build used (ids saved with the generation), else the latest for its series and market.

Dixi helps a BMW product manager turn what each market says into car profiles for the next 1, 5 or 7 Series, and keeps the reason for every decision. Inputs sit in three layers: **L1 BMW principles** (series fundamentals plus market and BMW Group principles from the team's public-source research, stored in Supabase; an AI principle assessor rates every request against them), **L2 market evidence** (customer feedback and feature requests, customer studies, sales, today's option list, plus a research agent that adds competitor features people like and market trends, each with sources) and **L3 social test** (runs only after profiles exist: which profile tracks better on social media; low weight per series: 7 Series 2 %, 5 Series 8 %, 1 Series 20 %). The PM picks a market and a series; a data script groups BMW's feedback into feature requests by category, rules set urgency, and the principle assessor adds each request's principle fit with evidence and assumptions kept apart; the PM keeps or rejects each one (a reject needs a reason), drags them into priority order and wishlists competitor or trend features. Dixi then builds three profiles that follow that priority (score = L1 principle fit + priority fit, plus L2 coverage) and saves the build as a **generation** with its profiles, decisions and priority. Every decision records who made it (name and role, from a simple local identity until there is a login) and when, and shows up in the decision log, the profile's decision trail and its PDF. With the backend connected, decisions (append-only), generations, settings and agent runs are stored in Supabase, and the next generation reads them as decision memory; without it, they stay in the browser. BMW customer text stays local and git-ignored (never sent to OpenAI or Supabase), and the public deployment runs on example data.

Title: Reasoning models
URL: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning

Highlights:
Start with `gpt-6-astra` for most reasoning workloads. For lower cost, consider `gpt-5.6-terra`, or `gpt-5.6-luna` for the lowest cost and latency. If you're using a GPT-5.6 or GPT-6 model, see reasoning mode for its `pro` option.
...
## Reasoning effort

The `reasoning.effort` parameter guides the model on how much to think when performing a task.

Supported values are model-dependent and can include `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. Lower effort favors speed and lower token usage, while at higher effort the model thinks more completely to provide higher quality responses. The models also reason adaptively across reasoning efforts, using fewer tokens for simpler tasks and thinking harder for complex tasks.

GPT-6 Astra does not support `none` reasoning
effort. Setting `reasoning.effort` (Responses) or `reasoning_effort` (Chat
Completions) to `none` returns HTTP 400. GPT-6.1 Sol
does not support `none` or `minimal` and defaults to `medium`.

Use the Responses API for function
calling. Chat Completions does not support function calling with GPT-6 Astra or
GPT-6.1 Sol.

Defaults are also model-dependent rather than universal. `gpt-5.5` defaults to `medium` reasoning effort. This is the best starting point for `gpt-5.5`’s full balance of quality, reliability and performance.
...
## Reasoning mode

GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 models support `standard` and `pro` reasoning modes in the Responses API. `standard` is the default. Set `reasoning.mode` to `pro` for difficult tasks that need more model work and can tolerate higher latency and token usage.

Reasoning mode and reasoning effort are independent. Mode selects standard or pro execution, while `reasoning.effort` controls how much reasoning the model applies within that mode. If you omit `reasoning.effort`, GPT-5.6 defaults to `medium` in both modes. GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna also default to `medium` reasoning effort.
...

curl https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

    "input": "Review this database migration plan and identify potential failure modes."
  }'
...

to `current_turn`. GPT-6.1 Sol also

Luna is the most cost-efficient model, while Astra is our state-of-the-art,
most powerful model. If cost and latency aren't a concern, you can default to
Astra. To reduce costs or latency, use the guidance below to choose a model
and reasoning effort for your needs.

1. Luna · Low Fine-grained edits, well-scoped problem-solving, and simple data extraction.
2. Luna · Extra high Finding current context across multiple apps, prioritizing work, and solving problems with clear constraints.
3. GPT-6.1 Sol · Medium Complex technical work and coordinated deliverables you expect to revise.
4. GPT-6.1 Sol · Extra high Polished deliverables, connected visual systems, and decisions built from conflicting evidence.
5. Astra · Low Concise writing and content adaptation that preserve facts and nuance.
6. Astra · Medium Ambitious projects that need broad context, reliable interactions, and complete results.
7. Astra · Extra high Demanding analysis and complex deliverables with exacting requirements.
...
Treat the guidance on this page as a starting point. The best way to find the right
model for your workflow is to experiment with different models and reasoning
settings to see what works.

content.text:
The chat is now a floating button at the bottom right of the profile page. Click it and a chat panel opens above it with the input ready; ✕ or Esc closes it. I checked it in the browser and pushed it.

**On your question: yes, every AI step uses OpenAI, and both models we use are OpenAI's reasoning models.** OpenAI's docs list both with reasoning-token support.

| Where | Model | Reasoning effort |
|---|---|---|
| Principle assessor (L1 fit, conflicts, assumptions) | `gpt-6.1-sol` | default **medium** (we don't set it) |
| Research agent: lead researcher | `gpt-6.1-sol` | default medium |
| Research agent: competitor and trend scouts | `gpt-6-luna` | default medium |
| Generation chat | `gpt-6-luna` | default medium |
| "Tell Dixi in your words" (settings) | `gpt-6-luna` (web route) | default medium |

The model names come from `OPENAI_MODEL_STRONG` and `OPENAI_MODEL_FAST` in `backend/.env`. All calls go through the Responses API, which OpenAI requires for tool calling with these models.

What OpenAI's docs say about these models:
- **`gpt-6.1-sol`** is described as balancing intelligence and cost. Its effort runs from low to max, and it doesn't support `none`.
- **`gpt-6-luna`** is described as the most cost-efficient.
- **`gpt-6-astra`** is the flagship reasoning model. We don't use it.

Sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning

There's one easy improvement. OpenAI's model-selection guide recommends Sol at extra-high effort for "decisions built from conflicting evidence". That matches our principle assessor exactly. Raising the assessor to `xhigh` is a one-line `model_settings` change and would likely improve its judgement, at the cost of more tokens and a slower analysis (it already takes about 50 s). Want me to set it, maybe just for the assessor?

**The OpenAI Decisions API, for labelling:** it doesn't write text. You give it an input and questions, and it answers with typed results:
- **`choice`:** one value from your list, with a confidence.
- **`predicate`:** the probability that a condition is true.
- **`score`:** a level on an ordered rubric.

It's in public beta, works only with `gpt-6-luna`, and uses its own endpoint, `POST /v1/decisions`. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions

Where it fits Dixi:

| Use | Question type | Sends BMW customer text? |
|---|---|---|
| **Label each customer comment**: which of the 25 requests it belongs to, which of the 4 categories, and whether it's a want, hard to use, or a defect. This could replace the fixed taxonomy mapping, or check it | `choice` (+ confidence) | **Yes**, needs BMW's OK |
| **Urgency or severity per comment** (e.g. 1 = cosmetic … 5 = safety or breakdown) | `score` | **Yes** |
| **Does this competitor or trend signal support this request?** A probability per pair, instead of the research agent guessing `relatesTo` | `predicate` | No, our own titles and public signals only |
| **Principle relevance per request × principle**: a measurable number instead of one overall judgement | `predicate` or `score` | No |

My recommendation:
- **Now:** use Decisions for **signal ↔ request matching**. It needs no customer data, gives a real probability with a threshold you choose, and makes the "market backing" part of the score measurable.
- **After BMW confirms that comments may go to OpenAI:** use it to **label the comments**, run inside the planned monthly job. Each label would keep its confidence, and low-confidence labels would go to the PM for review. That is exactly the labelling you had in mind.

Should I build the signal-matching part now, and document comment labelling as the next step once BMW confirms?

content.text:
Yes, that's the right design: a script that runs once a month, labels the new data with the Decisions API, and stores the result. The app then reads that result, and the PM still makes every decision. This is how I'd structure it:

```
monthly-refresh   (GitHub Actions: schedule cron "0 3 1 * *" → 03:00 on the 1st, or run by hand)
│
├─ 1. Load      the latest BMW export (feedback, studies, sales) for each series
├─ 2. Label     each new comment with the Decisions API (gpt-6-luna)
│     • choice    → which of the 25 feature requests (or "other / new")
│     • choice    → Exterior · Interior · Digital · Powertrain
│     • choice    → want · hard to use · defect
│     • score     → severity 1–5 (cosmetic … safety)
│     each label keeps its confidence; low confidence → "needs review"
├─ 3. Aggregate mention counts per request × market, with the month
│                 (so the resurfacing rule sees demand growth over time)
├─ 4. Research  run the research agent for all 9 series × market combinations
│     • predicate → "does this signal support this request?" (probability)
├─ 5. Assess    re-run the principle assessor on the refreshed requests
└─ 6. Report    store a "what changed" summary in Supabase:
                new / grown requests, new signals, resurfaced rejects,
                labels that need review → the PM sees it on the dashboard
```

Why it works well:
- **Typed and measurable:** every label is a fixed value with a confidence, not free text. You can check a sample by hand and set thresholds.
- **Traceable:** each label stores the model, the date, the question and the confidence. A request's count can be traced back to labelled comments.
- **Cheap and fast:** OpenAI says Decisions is about 10× faster than the Responses API, and it uses the lowest-cost model, so a few thousand comments a month is realistic. *(inferred; I haven't checked the pricing)*
- **Human in the loop:** the job only proposes. Low-confidence labels and new clusters go to the PM for review.

Two things to settle before it runs on real data:
1. **BMW's consent.** Step 2 sends customer comments to OpenAI, which Dixi deliberately never does today. Until BMW agrees, the script can run in a **dry-run mode**: label a small sample locally, compare it with the current taxonomy mapping, and send nothing at scale.
2. **Where the BMW export comes from each month.** Today it's a file in `data/`. In production it would be a secure drop or an API from BMW. The job needs that input.

Should I build it now as `backend/scripts/monthly_refresh.py`? That would be the 6 steps with a `--dry-run` default that sends nothing, plus a GitHub Actions workflow file that is present but disabled until you switch it on, tests with a fake Decisions client, and the docs updated.

    path = DATA / "bmw" / "feedback" / f"{series}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx"
    df = pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name="Feedback_Explorer", dtype=str)
    df["market"] = df["Country"].map(market_of)
    for col in ("Vfc level2 Name", "Vfc level3 Name", "Feedback Type", "Customer Feedback", "Source"):
        df[col] = df[col].fillna("").str.strip()
    return df


def cluster_key(l2: str, l3: str) -> str | None:
    if not l2 or l2 == "no_class_found":
        return None
    if (l2, l3) in L2L3_OVERRIDES:
        return L2L3_OVERRIDES[(l2, l3)]
    if l2 in CATCH_ALL_DEFAULT:
        return CATCH_ALL_DEFAULT[l2]
    return TOPIC_TO_GROUP.get(l2, "topic:" + l2)


def negative_rows(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    neg = df[df["Feedback Type"].isin(NEG_TYPES)].copy()
    neg["type"] = neg["Feedback Type"].map(NEG_TYPES)
    # Unclassified survey rows (sources C/D) only when they carry a VFC topic with a negative aspect.
    extra = df[(df["Feedback Type"] == "") & df["Source"].isin(["Source C", "Source D"])
               & (df["Vfc level2 Name"] != "") & (df["Vfc level2 Name"] != "no_class_found")
               & df["Vfc level3 Name"].isin(["Not user-friendly", "Malfunction", "Damage", "Noise"])].copy()
    extra["type"] = extra["Vfc level3 Name"].map(lambda x: "difficult" if x == "Not user-friendly" else "defect")
    out = pd.concat([neg, extra], ignore_index=True)
    out["cluster"] = [cluster_key(a, b) for a, b in zip(out["Vfc level2 Name"], out["Vfc level3 Name"])]
    return out[out["cluster"].notna()]


ARTEFACTS = re.compile(r"[▶►•■□◆★☆→※]|[\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF☀-➿]")

input.content:
"""Monthly refresh: label new customer comments, count demand per request and market, compare with last month,
optionally re-run research and the principle assessor, and report what changed for the PM.

    load comments ─▶ label (taxonomy rules | OpenAI Decisions API) ─▶ aggregate ─▶ compare with last run
                 ─▶ [research agent per series × market] ─▶ [principle assessor] ─▶ report (+ store in Supabase)

Labels, per comment (Decisions API question types):
  request    choice    which existing feature request it belongs to, or "other" (new / unclear)
  category   choice    Exterior · Interior · Digital · Powertrain
  type       choice    want · difficult · defect · praise
  severity   score     cosmetic … safety (0–4, probability-weighted)
Each choice comes with a confidence; low confidence or "other" puts the comment in the review queue. The job proposes;
the PM decides. Comment text is used only to label and is never stored (feedback_labels holds ids and labels).
CLI: backend/scripts/monthly_refresh.py · docs: docs/architecture/10-backend-agents.md §0.
"""
import asyncio
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable, Protocol

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from app.models.core import ScoringSettings
from app.scoring import build_memory

CATEGORIES = ["Exterior", "Interior", "Digital", "Powertrain"]
TYPES = {
    "want": "Asks for something that is missing or should be better",
    "difficult": "Says something is hard or confusing to use",
    "defect": "Reports something broken, faulty or unreliable",
    "praise": "Says something is good; no request",
}
SEVERITY = [
    ("cosmetic", "Looks or feels slightly off; no effect on use"),
    ("annoying", "Irritates regularly but the car works"),
    ("hinders use", "Makes a feature hard to use or avoid"),
    ("breakdown", "A function fails or the car must go to the workshop"),
    ("safety", "Could affect safety"),
]
OTHER = "other"


@dataclass
class Comment:
    id: str
    series: str
    market: str
    text: str
    #: Request id from BMW's taxonomy mapping (data script), when known: used by the rules labeler and to compare.
    taxonomy_request: str | None = None
    #: Feedback type from the BMW export, when known.
    taxonomy_type: str | None = None


@dataclass
class RequestDef:
    id: str
    series: str
    title: str
    category: str
    summary: str = ""


class Label(BaseModel):
    comment_id: str
    series: str
    market: str
    request_id: str | None
    request_conf: float | None = None
    category: str | None = None
    category_conf: float | None = None
    feedback_type: str | None = None
    type_conf: float | None = None
    severity: float | None = None
    severity_label: str | None = None
    needs_review: bool = False


class Labeler(Protocol):
    name: str

    async def label(self, comments: list[Comment], catalog: list[RequestDef]) -> list[Label]: ...


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ labelers


class TaxonomyLabeler:
    """Today's rules: the request comes from BMW's taxonomy mapping. No network; the dry-run default."""

    name = "taxonomy"

    async def label(self, comments, catalog):
        by_id = {r.id: r for r in catalog}
        out = []
        for c in comments:
            r = by_id.get(c.taxonomy_request or "")
            out.append(Label(comment_id=c.id, series=c.series, market=c.market, request_id=r.id if r else None,
                             request_conf=1.0 if r else None, category=r.category if r else None,
                             category_conf=1.0 if r else None, feedback_type=c.taxonomy_type,
                             type_conf=1.0 if c.taxonomy_type else None, needs_review=r is None))
        return out


class DecisionsLabeler:
    """OpenAI Decisions API (POST /v1/decisions): typed answers with confidences. Sends each comment's text to OpenAI,
    so it runs only when the operator passes --send (BMW must have agreed)."""

    def __init__(self, client: Any, model: str = "gpt-6-luna", review_below: float = 0.6, concurrency: int = 8):
        self.client, self.model, self.review_below = client, model, review_below
        self.sem = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)
        self.name = f"decisions:{model}"
        self.calls = 0

    def questions(self, catalog: list[RequestDef]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        return [
            {"type": "choice", "name": "request",
             "instructions": "Which of these existing BMW feature requests does the customer comment belong to? "
                             "Choose 'other' if none fits or the comment asks for something new.",
             "choices": [{"value": r.id, "description": f"{r.title}. {r.summary}".strip()} for r in catalog]
             + [{"value": OTHER, "description": "None of the above, or a new topic"}]},
            {"type": "choice", "name": "category", "instructions": "Which part of the car is the comment about?",
             "choices": [{"value": c, "description": c} for c in CATEGORIES]},
            {"type": "choice", "name": "type", "instructions": "What kind of feedback is it?",
             "choices": [{"value": k, "description": v} for k, v in TYPES.items()]},
            {"type": "score", "name": "severity", "instructions": "How severe is the issue for the customer?",
             "levels": [{"label": k, "description": v} for k, v in SEVERITY]},
        ]

    async def _one(self, c: Comment, catalog: list[RequestDef]) -> Label:
        series_catalog = [r for r in catalog if r.series == c.series] or catalog
        async with self.sem:
            self.calls += 1
            d = await self.client.decisions.create(model=self.model, input=c.text, questions=self.questions(series_catalog))
        a = {x.name: x for x in d.answers}

        def choice(name: str) -> tuple[str | None, float | None]:
            x = a.get(name)
            return (str(x.choice), x.confidence) if x is not None and x.type == "choice" else (None, None)

        req, req_conf = choice("request")
        cat, cat_conf = choice("category")
        typ, typ_conf = choice("type")
        sev = a.get("severity")
        sev_val = sev.score if sev is not None and sev.type == "score" else None
        sev_label = max(sev.probabilities, key=lambda p: p.probability).label if sev_val is not None else None
        refused = any(x.type == "refusal" for x in d.answers)
        unsure = req in (None, OTHER) or (req_conf or 0) < self.review_below or refused
        return Label(comment_id=c.id, series=c.series, market=c.market, request_id=None if req in (None, OTHER) else req,
                     request_conf=req_conf, category=cat, category_conf=cat_conf, feedback_type=typ, type_conf=typ_conf,
                     severity=sev_val, severity_label=sev_label, needs_review=unsure)

    async def label(self, comments, catalog):
        return list(await asyncio.gather(*(self._one(c, catalog) for c in comments)))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ aggregate, compare, report


def aggregate(labels: list[Label]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Mentions per request: total, per market, per feedback type, mean severity."""
    out: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    sev: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
    for lab in labels:
        if not lab.request_id:
            continue
        row = out.setdefault(lab.request_id, {"series": lab.series, "mentions": 0, "byMarket": Counter(), "types": Counter()})
        row["mentions"] += 1
        row["byMarket"][lab.market] += 1
        if lab.feedback_type:
            row["types"][lab.feedback_type] += 1
        if lab.severity is not None:
            sev[lab.request_id].append(lab.severity)
    for rid, row in out.items():
        row["byMarket"], row["types"] = dict(row["byMarket"]), dict(row["types"])
        row["severity"] = round(sum(sev[rid]) / len(sev[rid]), 2) if sev[rid] else None
    return out


def compare(prev: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None, now: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], grow_at: float = 0.3) -> dict[str, list]:
    prev = prev or {}
    new = sorted(r for r in now if r not in prev)
    grown = sorted(
        ({"request": r, "before": prev[r]["mentions"], "now": now[r]["mentions"],
          "growth": round((now[r]["mentions"] - prev[r]["mentions"]) / prev[r]["mentions"], 2)}

    """Mentions per request: total, per market, per feedback type, mean severity."""
    out: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    sev: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
    for lab in labels:
        if not lab.request_id:
            continue
        row = out.setdefault(lab.request_id, {"series": lab.series, "mentions": 0, "byMarket": Counter(), "types": Counter()})
        row["mentions"] += 1
        row["byMarket"][lab.market] += 1
        if lab.feedback_type:
            row["types"][lab.feedback_type] += 1
        if lab.severity is not None:
            sev[lab.request_id].append(lab.severity)
    for rid, row in out.items():
        row["byMarket"], row["types"] = dict(row["byMarket"]), dict(row["types"])
        row["severity"] = round(sum(sev[rid]) / len(sev[rid]), 2) if sev[rid] else None
    return out


def compare(prev: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None, now: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], grow_at: float = 0.3) -> dict[str, list]:
    prev = prev or {}
    new = sorted(r for r in now if r not in prev)
    grown = sorted(
        ({"request": r, "before": prev[r]["mentions"], "now": now[r]["mentions"],
          "growth": round((now[r]["mentions"] - prev[r]["mentions"]) / prev[r]["mentions"], 2)}
         for r in now if r in prev and prev[r]["mentions"] and (now[r]["mentions"] - prev[r]["mentions"]) / prev[r]["mentions"] >= grow_at),
        key=lambda x: -x["growth"])
    dropped = sorted(r for r in prev if r not in now)
    return {"new": new, "grown": grown, "dropped": dropped}


def resurfaced(generations: list[dict[str, Any]], counts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], catalog: list[RequestDef],
               settings: ScoringSettings) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Rejected requests whose demand in that market grew past the team's resurface threshold since the reject."""
    titles = {r.id: r for r in catalog}
    out = []
    for (series, market) in {(g.get("series"), g.get("scope")) for g in generations}:
        mem = build_memory(generations, series, market, settings)
        for rid, row in counts.items():
            r = titles.get(rid)
            if not r or r.series != series:
                continue
            m = mem.get(f"{series}:{r.title.lower()}")
            n = row["byMarket"].get(market, 0)
            if m and m.action == "reject" and m.mentionsAt and (n - m.mentionsAt) / m.mentionsAt >= settings.resurfaceAt:
                out.append({"request": r.title, "series": series, "market": market, "rejected_at": m.at,
                            "reason": m.reason, "mentions_then": m.mentionsAt, "mentions_now": n})
    return out


class RefreshReport(BaseModel):
    month: str
    labeler: str
    source: str
    comments: int
    labelled: int
    needs_review: int
    review_queue: list[str] = Field(description="Comment ids to check by hand (low confidence or no fitting request)")
    agreement_with_taxonomy: float | None = Field(default=None, description="Share of comments where the labeler picked the taxonomy's request")
    counts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
    changes: dict[str, list]
    resurfaced: list[dict[str, Any]]
    research_runs: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    assessments: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    generatedAt: str


@dataclass
class RefreshDeps:
    store: Any | None = None
    #: async (series, market, request_titles) -> research run id
    research: Callable[[str, str, list[str]], Awaitable[str | None]] | None = None
    #: async (series, market, counts for that series) -> assessment id
    assess: Callable[[str, str, list[dict[str, Any]]], Awaitable[str | None]] | None = None
    markets: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["EU", "US", "CN"])


async def run_refresh(comments: list[Comment], catalog: list[RequestDef], labeler: Labeler, *, month: str, source: str,
                      deps: RefreshDeps | None = None, store_results: bool = False) -> tuple[RefreshReport, list[Label]]:
    deps = deps or RefreshDeps()
    labels = await labeler.label(comments, catalog)
    counts = aggregate(labels)

    prev = await deps.store.latest_refresh() if deps.store else None
    changes = compare(prev["report"]["counts"] if prev else None, counts)
    res: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if deps.store:
        settings = (await deps.store.get_settings()).settings
        gens = [g.payload for g in await deps.store.list_generations()]
        res = resurfaced(gens, counts, catalog, settings)

    known = [c for c in comments if c.taxonomy_request]
    agree = None
    if known and labeler.name != "taxonomy":
        by = {lab.comment_id: lab for lab in labels}
        agree = round(sum(1 for c in known if by[c.id].request_id == c.taxonomy_request) / len(known), 3)

    research_ids, assessment_ids = [], []
    titles = {r.id: r.title for r in catalog}
    for series in sorted({r.series for r in catalog}):
        for market in deps.markets:
            if deps.research:
                rid = await deps.research(series, market, [r.title for r in catalog if r.series == series])
                if rid:
                    research_ids.append(rid)
            if deps.assess:
                rows = [{"id": rid, "title": titles[rid], "mentions": row["byMarket"].get(market, 0)}
                        for rid, row in counts.items() if row["series"] == series and row["byMarket"].get(market)]
                if rows:
                    aid = await deps.assess(series, market, rows)
                    if aid:
                        assessment_ids.append(aid)

    report = RefreshReport(
        month=month, labeler=labeler.name, source=source, comments=len(comments),
        labelled=sum(1 for lab in labels if lab.request_id), needs_review=sum(1 for lab in labels if lab.needs_review),
        review_queue=[lab.comment_id for lab in labels if lab.needs_review], agreement_with_taxonomy=agree,
        counts=counts, changes=changes, resurfaced=res, research_runs=research_ids, assessments=assessment_ids,
        generatedAt=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
    )
    if store_results and deps.store:
        await deps.store.save_refresh({"month": month, "labeler": labeler.name, "source": source,
                                       "report": report.model_dump(mode="json")},
                                      [lab.model_dump() for lab in labels])
    return report, labels

def build_requests(series: str, df: pd.DataFrame, options: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    neg = negative_rows(df)
    sizes = neg.groupby("cluster")["ID"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
    keep = [k for k, n in sizes.items() if n >= MIN_MENTIONS][:MAX_REQUESTS]
    reqs = []
    for key in keep:
        rows = neg[neg["cluster"] == key]
        ids = rows["ID"].unique()
        group = GROUPS.get(key)
        if group:
            title, category, lead = group["title"], group["category"], group["lead"]
        else:
            topic = key.split(":", 1)[1]
            title = f"Improve {topic.lower()}"
            category = fallback_category(topic)
            lead = f"Owners raise issues with {topic.lower()}"
        types = {t: int(rows[rows["type"] == t]["ID"].nunique()) for t in ("wants", "difficult", "defect")}
        l3 = rows[rows["Vfc level3 Name"] != ""].groupby("Vfc level3 Name")["ID"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
        aspects = [l3_phrase(a) for a in l3.index[:2]]
        total_t = sum(types.values()) or 1
        split = ", ".join(
            f"{round(100 * types[t] / total_t)}% {label}"
            for t, label in (("wants", "wishes"), ("difficult", "difficult to use"), ("defect", "defects"))
            if types[t]
        )
        aspect_txt = " and ".join(dict.fromkeys(aspects)) if aspects else "general issues"
        summary = f"{lead}; the main themes are {aspect_txt} ({split})."
        combos = (rows.assign(c=rows["Vfc level2 Name"] + " : " + rows["Vfc level3 Name"])
                  [rows["Vfc level3 Name"] != ""].groupby("c")["ID"].nunique()
                  .sort_values(ascending=False))
        taxonomy = list(combos.index[:4])
        if not taxonomy:
            taxonomy = list(rows["Vfc level2 Name"].value_counts().index[:4])
        by_market = rows.drop_duplicates("ID")["market"].value_counts().to_dict()
        src = rows.groupby("Source")["ID"].nunique().sort_index()
        reqs.append({
            "id": "",
            "series": series,
            "title": title,
            "category": category,
            "summary": summary,
            "mentions": int(len(ids)),
            "byMarket": ordered_markets(by_market),
            "types": types,
            "sources": [{"name": s, "count": int(c)} for s, c in src.items()],
            "quotes": pick_quotes(rows),
            "taxonomy": taxonomy,
            "relatedOptions": match_options(key if group else None, options),
        })
    reqs.sort(key=lambda r: (-r["mentions"], r["title"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(reqs, 1):
        r["id"] = f"{series}-R{i:02d}"
    return reqs
